You are Lane C of the SuperGrok1.5 H100 megakernel campaign, working in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. STRICT CONSTRAINT: CPU-ONLY — do not run anything on the GPU (no CUDA-initializing python, no tests that launch kernels). Compiling with nvcc is fine. Another lane owns the GPU; your GPU-runnable tests will be executed later from a RUNBOOK you write.

MISSION: finish the Phase-2 (multi-GPU) authoring as far as it can go on one GPU's worth of hardware, so the 8×H100 rental window is validate-and-measure only. The standing definition (owner's provisioning rule): 8× gets provisioned when the parallelism TEMPLATE + DP/ZeRO/PP/TP code is AUTHORED and single-GPU-unit-tested as far as possible — only NVSHMEM-TP transport validation and real scaling measurements may remain for the 8×.

REQUIRED CONTEXT (read first):
- /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §7 (parallelism design contract)
- Commit ef433ac ("phase-2 pre-tests: sharded-opt bit-parity + DP=2 loopback cross-rank A/A/A + step graph capture") — read the diff and the test files it added; 16/16 of these pre-tests are green on hardware as of last night.
- /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/HANDOFF.md, csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md
- /root/.claude/projects/-workspace-SuperGrok1-5/memory/h100-durable-requirements.md and no-functionality-suppression.md

ENVIRONMENT: export SCCACHE_DIR=/dev/shm/sccache TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp. 224 cores, sm_90a target. Another lane is editing csrc/bindings/* and grokking_optimizers/compile.py concurrently — avoid those files entirely.

JOB:
1. INVENTORY: build an authored-vs-missing matrix across DP / ZeRO-1 / ZeRO-2 / ZeRO-3 / PP / TP against the §7 contract. What exists (ParConfig, sharded-opt, shard-map, DP loopback, graph capture), what's stubbed, what's absent.
2. AUTHOR the missing pieces, deepest-single-GPU-testable-first:
   - TP via NVSHMEM: check whether nvshmem headers/libs are installed (find / -name "nvshmem*" etc.). If yes, author the real transport + compile it. If no, author the TP layer against the contract's transport interface with a BIT-EXACT single-process loopback transport implementation (same code path, memcpy/symmetric-heap-simulated), clearly marked as the transport swap point — the loopback must be honestly testable, NOT fake success. The TP math (column/row-parallel megakernel tiling, all-reduce points in the fused step) is the durable part; author it for real.
   - PP: the pipeline schedule (1F1B or interleaved — follow the §7 contract), stage partitioning of the megakernel step, activation hand-off buffers, and a single-GPU 2-stage loopback test (both stages on one device, A/A/A bit-exactness across a virtual boundary like ef433ac did for DP).
   - ZeRO-3: parameter partitioning + gather/release around the fused step, sharded optimizer state checkpoint/save-resume round-trip (bit-exact), building on the existing sharded-opt parity work.
3. TESTS: write the single-GPU tests for everything above in the same style/location as ef433ac's pre-tests, but DO NOT RUN them. Write /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/RUNBOOK.md: exact commands, expected pass criteria, expected wall-time, what each test proves, and the residual list of things that GENUINELY need 8 GPUs.
4. COMMITS: you may commit NEW files only (git add each explicit new path; nothing tracked-modified), message tagged "#25 phase-2 authoring", local only, never push. If the git index is locked (another lane committing), wait 30s and retry. Any change you need in an EXISTING tracked file goes into /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/*.patch instead, with a note in the report.

RULES: no functionality suppression; the megakernel step stays the unit of execution (don't decompose it back into ops to make sharding easier — shard AROUND the fused step per the contract); honest stubs only, loudly marked.

DELIVERABLE: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/REPORT.md with the matrix, what you authored, compile proof, the RUNBOOK, and the genuinely-needs-8× residual list. Your final message: the matrix summary, file list, nvshmem-found verdict, and what's left — raw facts, not prose.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Author: peterc04 <pcoy400@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 12 14:33:33 2026 +0000

    phase-2 pre-tests: sharded-opt bit-parity + DP=2 loopback cross-rank A/A/A + step graph capture (#25, design §7)
    
    DELIVERABLE 1 (§7.3) tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py + sharded_optimizer_binding.cu:
    at DP=1, sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> over the full param set is BIT-IDENTICAL
    (maxd=0, params + m/v state) to the in-kernel P3 fused tail on the same (params,
    grad, state). The equivalent check: run the production fused step (return_grad), then
    re-apply via the JIT-bound sharded kernel on the captured grad + zero state + the
    same _opt_scalars_from scalars. Elementwise ids {adamw,lion,grokfast} x {decoder,vit,
    mamba} = 9 cells, all bit-exact. JIT-bound via cpp_extension.load into /workspace/
    .torch_ext (own build dir; production _ops untouched).
    
    DELIVERABLE 2 (§7.1+§6.4 at DP=2) tests/hw/test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py:
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=2, both ranks on cuda:0 (distinct NCCL_HOSTID defeats NCCL
    2.20.5's duplicate-GPU dedup). Each rank runs the production fused step on its batch
    shard; fixed-order all_gather+ascending-rank fp32 reduce of grad (the §2.7/§6.4 A/A/A
    non-negotiable, not raw NCCL reduce-scatter); sharded-opt over the owned shard;
    all_gather params. Asserts (a) cross-rank params identical, (b) 3x A/A/A bit-identical,
    (c) vs single-GPU unsharded within parity tol (measured rel: adamw 6.6e-6, lion 0,
    grokfast 1.1e-5, vit-adamw 1.2e-5 < 3e-5). 4 cells green.
    
    DELIVERABLE 3 (§7.4) tests/hw/test_step_graph_capture.py: capture [ops.fused_step ->
    sharded_optimizer_kernel] as ONE CUDA graph (rank 0 stream), replay 5x, each bit-
    identical to eager (maxd=0). The persistent megakernel captures fine. NOT captured on
    this 1-GPU loopback: the megakernel mixed with NCCL collectives across two ranks on
    one device (collective-vs-megakernel SM contention; the eager path needed explicit
    syncs between every megakernel and collective). Per-piece each captures (fused-step,
    sharded-opt, standalone NCCL all_gather all verified); only the mixed cross-rank
    lockstep is the irreducible 8-GPU work (§7.5). Documented in the file.
    
    GATES: 16/16 new tests green on 1xH100; production _ops untouched (wiring_check
    --require-all 33/33 L3-TC); tree clean except the new files.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1	# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)
2	
3	Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
4	all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
5	and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
6	headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
7	meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
8	only composition seam.
9	
10	## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)
11	
12	| component | header(s) | contract |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
15	| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
16	| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
17	| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
18	| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
19	| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
20	| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |
21	
22	## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
23	1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
24	   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
25	2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
26	   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
27	   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
28	3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
29	   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
30	   correct (if untuned) kernel.
31	4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
32	   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
33	   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
34	   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
35	   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
36	5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
37	   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
38	6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
39	   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
40	   dispatch.

1	# SuperGrok L3-TC Parallelism Layer — Phase-2 Contract (4D + ZeRO-3, owner-locked)
2	
3	**Status:** DESIGN-ONLY (task #22). Written CPU-only, no repo edits, no build, no GPU.
4	**Author context:** grounded in a read-through of the actual kernel + dispatch stack (file refs below). Speculative claims are marked **[SPEC]**; frontier-risk items are marked **[FRONTIER]**.
5	**Supersedes for the *kernel-level* template:** the prior Stage-7 "Python-orchestration-only, DeepSpeed/Megatron adapter, no-kernel-changes" design in `grokking_optimizers/distributed.py` + `megakernel_engine.py` + `tests/hw/test_3d_parallel.py`. That layer is **reused** (rank mesh, ZeRO-3 shard math, NCCL bootstrap) but is **not sufficient**: the owner locked a *metaprogrammed template over the megakernel itself* with device-initiated NVSHMEM TP and a graph-captured step. This doc specifies the new compile-time-config + in-kernel-comm increments and tells you exactly which existing pieces to keep.
6	
7	This doc is the Phase-2 contract: it is what an author + a kernel builder execute against once the owner provisions 8×H100. Every choice is tied to the locked decisions in `/workspace/.campaign_plan.md` ("PARALLELISM DECISION — FINAL", "#14 FINDING", "#14 FIT-CEILING").
8	
9	**DELIVERABLE — LOCKED (owner clarification 2026-06-12, supersedes any contrary language below): the flagship ships as FULL 4D+ZeRO-3 — DP×TP×PP all ACTIVE (SP axis expressible in the template, pinned 1 at seq 4-17), ZeRO stage 3, max batch, all three models.** The increments in this doc (DP+ZeRO-2 → ZeRO-3 → +PP → +TP) are the **BRING-UP ORDER ONLY** — each validates one layer of machinery in isolation so failures are attributable; ZeRO-2 is ZeRO-3-minus-param-sharding (same code, a stage flag), nothing is built-then-discarded. **They are NOT off-ramps:** no kill-gate below may demote the flagship to a lesser config. Per-dimension throughput contributions are MEASURED and REPORTED honestly (the owner heard the ≤13B throughput dissent and chose the maximal system), but every dimension ships. The ONE genuine go/no-go in this design is the **TP implementation** — device-initiated NVSHMEM (stretch) vs host-NCCL TP (fallback) — and BOTH are TP, so 4D ships either way.

11	---
12	
13	## 0. Ground truth — what is actually on disk (the things every choice below rests on)
14	
15	Read these before changing anything; the design is shaped to them, not to a generic transformer.
16	
17	### 0.1 The single-GPU megakernel (the asset we wrap, never split on the inside without NVSHMEM)
18	`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` — two kernels:
19	- **scalar** `fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>` (default, fp32 owner-computes), launcher `launch_fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>` (`:272`).
20	- **wgmma** `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`:431`), launcher `launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`:1081`), compiled only under `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1`.
21	
22	Phase/barrier layout of the **TC** kernel (the production path), all separated by the hand-built `GridBarrier` (`csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh:147`, CTA-count-agnostic, NO cooperative launch):
23	- **P0** zero per-CTA LN-vec partials + loss slot → `bar.sync()` (B0).
24	- **P1** token-tile-parallel **fwd+bwd through ALL layers, barrier-free within a tile** (`dectc_forward_tile`/`dectc_backward_tile`, `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh`). Each CTA grid-strides over `kTileM=128`-row token tiles. Per-token linear inputs `X` and output adjoints `dY` are streamed to an **HBM bf16 `DecActs` buffer** (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:180`), NOT kept resident. → `bar.sync()` (B1).
25	- **P2** deterministic grad assembly: dW **output-stationary** (`tile_id % nCTA` owns a weight-matrix tile, contracts full token dim `K=T`, ascending-`t`, **no float atomics**), optional **split-K G=4** over the ~62% idle SMs (`dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk`, ascending-chunk reduce), biases folded into the dY stream, embeddings owner-scan, LN-vec ascending-CTA reduce. → `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (B2) — **this is the seam.**
26	- **P2.4 / P2.5 / P2.6 / P2.7 / P2.45 / P3-SG2** the optimizer-specific in-kernel stages (see §0.4).
27	- **P3** the optimizer apply tail: work-steal the 30 tensors, `apply_optimizer<Opt>` (the canonical `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` math).
28	
29	**Why this matters for parallelism:** B2 is a clean cut. Everything before it is **fwd+bwd → reduced local grad in `grad[total]`**; everything after is **optimizer-over-grad → updated `params`**. The owner's locked multi-GPU decomposition (`/workspace/.campaign_plan.md:133-134`) cuts **exactly here**: `[fwd+bwd megakernel]  →  reduce-scatter(grad)  →  [sharded optimizer kernel]  →  all-gather(params)`.
30	
31	### 0.2 The grad/param/state ABI (what reduce-scatter & all-gather move)
32	- `params` = flat `float[total]` concat of `named_parameters()` order. `total = kDecTotalElems` (`decoder_layout.cuh:31`; at the d=2048 benchmark scale = 25,401,443; the small race scale is `kDecoderTotalElems` mirrored host-side in `dispatch.cpp:518`). **Regenerated per size-ladder tier** by the campaign's codegen.
33	- `grad` = flat `float[total]`, parallel to `params`. Returned through the ABI tensor (`dispatch.cpp:531`).
34	- per-tensor `kDecOffsets[30]` / `kDecSizes[30]` live in `__constant__` tables (`decoder_layout.cuh:34/41`), read directly by P2/P3 — **the host passes no layout tensors.**
35	- optimizer state = `state` tensor, layout `[m | v | extra] + loss` = `3*total+1` for most; **larger** for prodigy (`4*total+4`), SG11/15 (`4*total+1+phi_pack`), SG2 (`(5+GH)*total+1`, `GH=4`) — see `dispatch.py:1845-1856`. The per-element shards (`exp_avg`, `exp_avg_sq`, `ema`, `mu`, `sharpness`, `sg2_slow`, `sg2_gru_state`, `param_init`) are flat blobs parallel to `params`; `rebase_state<Opt>` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:123`) offsets them per tensor.

37	### 0.3 The orchestration entry to make rank-aware
38	`grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py::fused_train_step(...)` (`:1714`) is the one-step entry: packs params→`flat`, packs inputs, calls `ops.fused_step(..., opt_only=False, gemm_impl=...)` (`:2196`), scatters `flat`→`p.data`, reads loss from `state[3*total]`. 41	From `apply_optimizer<Opt>` (`opt_components.cuh:383`) + the in-kernel stages in `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc`:
42	
43	| Optimizer | OptId | State shape | Shards under ZeRO over the flat param? | Special global/structured op |
44	|---|---|---|---|---|
45	| adamw | 0 | m,v elementwise | **trivial** (elementwise) | none |
46	| lion | 1 | m elementwise | **trivial** | none |
47	| grokfast | 2 | m,ema elementwise | **trivial** | none |
48	| grokadamw | 3 | m,v,ema elementwise | **trivial elementwise** BUT | **GLOBAL grad-norm clip** (P2.5, `:710`) → one scalar all-reduce of Σg² |
49	| looksam | 4 | m,v,sam_dir elementwise | **trivial elementwise** BUT | **GLOBAL ‖g‖** (P2.4, `:588`) + a **2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd** at perturbed weights |

(b) The per-TENSOR optimizer constraint (§0.4) is **not modeled** by `_even_partition` (it splits mid-tensor). (c) TP/PP are config fields with **no kernel realization**. (d) No graph capture. (e) No NVSHMEM.

68	## 1. The compile-time parallelism config (the metaprogrammed template)
69	
70	### 1.1 The config struct + template parameter pack
71	New header `csrc/fused/sm_90/parallel_config.cuh` (device+host, header-only, included by every megakernel TU):
72	
73	```cpp
74	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace par {
75	
76	enum class ZeROStage : int { Z0 = 0, Z1 = 1, Z2 = 2, Z3 = 3 };
77	
78	// Compile-time parallelism point. ALL fields are constexpr so every branch that
79	// reads them folds at compile time -> the degenerate config emits ZERO comm code.
80	template <int DP, int TP, int PP, int SP, ZeROStage Z>
81	struct ParConfig {
82	    static constexpr int  kDP = DP;   // data-parallel replicas
83	    static constexpr int  kTP = TP;   // tensor-parallel ranks (Megatron col/row split)
84	    static constexpr int  kPP = PP;   // pipeline stages
85	    static constexpr int  kSP = SP;   // sequence-parallel (kept EXPRESSIBLE, fixed 1)
86	    static constexpr ZeROStage kZeRO = Z;
87	
88	    static constexpr bool kIsSingleGPU = (DP==1 && TP==1 && PP==1 && SP==1);
89	    static constexpr bool kEmitComm    = !kIsSingleGPU;       // gate ALL NVSHMEM/NCCL
90	    static constexpr bool kShardParams = (Z == ZeROStage::Z3);
91	    static constexpr bool kShardOptGrad= (Z >= ZeROStage::Z2);
92	    static constexpr bool kTPComm      = (TP > 1);            // in-kernel allreduce
93	    static constexpr bool kPPStage     = (PP > 1);
94	
95	    static_assert(SP == 1, "SP axis is expressible but must be 1 this campaign "
96	                           "(seq 4-17 makes a seq split moot; #14 / PARALLELISM-FINAL).");
97	    static_assert(DP>=1 && TP>=1 && PP>=1 && SP>=1, "degrees must be >= 1");
98	};
99	
100	// THE single-GPU guarantee, named once so the static_assert reads cleanly.
101	using SingleGPU = ParConfig<1,1,1,1, ZeROStage::Z0>;
102	
103	}}}  // sg::fused::par
104	```

134	### 2.1 The decomposed step (DP + ZeRO-2/3, the first increments — NO TP/PP yet)
135	```
136	per rank r, per step:
137	  [0] (ZeRO-3 only) all-gather params for the layers this rank will run  ── §3
138	  [1] fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, Par> launch  ── runs P0..B2, produces grad[total] LOCAL (this rank's batch shard)
139	        ── the kernel STOPS at B2 if kShardOptGrad (do NOT run P3 in-kernel under ZeRO)  ── §2.2
140	  [2] reduce-scatter(grad)  over the DP group  ── each rank ends with reduced grad for its OWNED shard only
141	  [3] sharded optimizer kernel  ── apply_optimizer<Opt> over the OWNED shard  ── §2.4
142	  [4] all-gather(params)  over the DP group  ── every rank gets full params for next step's fwd  (ZeRO-3)
143	                                                or no-op (ZeRO-2, params already replicated)
144	```

146	The whole `[1]..[4]` sequence is **CUDA-graph captured** as one replayable unit (§2.6).

148	### 2.2 Where the kernel is cut: a compile-time early-exit at B2
149	The megakernel does **not** physically split into two binaries. Instead, P3 (and the P2.x optimizer stages) become **`if constexpr (!Par::kShardOptGrad)`**-gated: when ZeRO≥2, the fused kernel **returns right after B2** (the reduced *local* grad is in `grad[total]`), and a **separate sharded-optimizer kernel** consumes the reduce-scattered grad. When ZeRO≤1, P3 runs in-kernel exactly as today (full fusion preserved for the DP+ZeRO-1 baseline).
150	
151	```cpp
152	// in fused_decoder_megakernel_tc, right after B2:
153	if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad) {
154	    // ZeRO-2/3: the optimizer runs in a SEPARATE kernel over the reduce-scattered,
155	    // SHARDED grad. The fused kernel's job ends at "local grad assembled".
156	    return;
157	}
158	// else: ZeRO-0/1 -> fall through to P2.4..P3 exactly as today (full fusion).
159	```
160	
161	This keeps the **single-GPU and DP+ZeRO-1 paths fully fused** (the novel artifact) while the ZeRO-2/3 multi-GPU path takes the clean cut. The owner's rule (`:133` "multi-GPU splits the opt off after the grad reduce-scatter — a clean cut at the existing opt barrier") is realized literally as this `if constexpr return`.

163	### 2.3 The sharded-optimizer kernel (new, small)
164	New header `csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh`:

168	    float* __restrict__ params_shard,   // [shard_numel] this rank's owned param slice
169	    const float* __restrict__ grad_shard,// [shard_numel] reduce-scattered grad
170	    float lr, int step, FusedOptState st_shard /* state ptrs pre-rebased to the shard */);

It is essentially P3 with the work-steal-over-30-tensors loop replaced by a flat grid-stride over the shard, and **no GridBarrier** (single phase). 181	  - **looksam**: global `‖g‖` → 1 float, same; **plus** the 2nd fwd+bwd must run on each rank's batch shard (it's a model recompute, naturally DP-parallel).
182	- **Per-MATRIX (muon):** the NS chain runs one 2D weight at a time across all CTAs (`:862`). Under ZeRO-3 the **whole matrix must live on one rank**; momentum `m` (the persistent buffer NS reads) must be **co-located with its matrix**. → tensor-granular shard.

185	### 2.5 Bucket / overlap strategy — can reduce-scatter overlap P2 dW?
186	**Yes, partially, and this is the highest-value overlap.** `#14 FINDING` (`/workspace/.campaign_plan.md:142`) established P2 (dW) leaves **~62% of SMs idle** at production batch (forward is SM-saturated, dW is not). The reduce-scatter is **comm**, not SM work, so it overlaps P2's compute for free on a separate stream/CUDA graph node. Concretely:
187	- **Per-tensor grad readiness:** P2 assembles grads **output-stationary per weight tile** in `kDecOffsets` order. As soon as a tensor's grad is fully assembled in `grad[off:off+n]`, it can be **bucketed and reduce-scattered** while later tensors are still being assembled. This is the megakernel analogue of DDP's per-bucket backward hooks (`distributed.py:595` already implements the hook pattern for the framework path — reuse the bucketization `_bucketize`, `distributed.py:188`).
188	- **Implementation [SPEC]:** because the megakernel is one launch, the cleanest first cut does **not** interleave comm inside the kernel — it lets the kernel finish (grad[total] complete at B2), then fires **one bucketed reduce-scatter** of ~`reduce_bucket_size` (25M elems default, `distributed.py:103`) on the comm stream, overlapping the **next** micro-batch's fwd if pipelined, or P3 if ZeRO-1. True intra-kernel comm/dW overlap is the **NVSHMEM frontier** (§5) — deferred.
189	- **Bucket recommendation:** at the d=2048/25.4M-param scale, the whole grad is ~one bucket (100 MB fp32). Reduce-scatter of 100 MB over NVLink (~400 GB/s effective) ≈ 0.25 ms; step wall at B=16384 is ~119 ms (`roofline.py:83`) → comm is **<0.3% of step**, so **bucketing/overlap is a second-order optimization at single-node scale.** It becomes load-bearing only at the 20-30B multi-node ceiling the owner targets (`:132`). **Build it, but don't gate the first increments on it.**

191	### 2.6 The CUDA-graph capture boundary
192	The owner **lifted the "No CUDA graphs" hard rule for the multi-GPU step only** (`/workspace/.campaign_plan.md:134`): single-GPU megakernel = NO graph (it IS the anti-graph); multi-GPU step = graph-captured.
193	- **Capture unit:** the `[1]..[4]` sequence (kernel launch → reduce-scatter → sharded-opt kernel → all-gather), captured once after warmup, replayed every step. This kills CPU launch jitter so the NCCL collectives issue back-to-back.
194	- **Boundary:** capture **excludes** the Python host work in `fused_train_step` (param pack-in/scatter-out, loss readback). Those become **pre/post-graph** copies; the graph operates on the persistent `flat`/`state`/`grad_out` buffers already cached across steps (`dispatch.py:1821`, the persistent-buffer discipline is **exactly what graph capture needs** — buffers must be stable-addressed). **This is a happy alignment: the existing state_cache reuse makes the step graph-capturable with no buffer-lifetime redesign.**
195	- **NCCL + graphs:** NCCL collectives are graph-capturable since NCCL 2.9 / CUDA 11.3; capture on the same stream the kernels use, with the comm stream joined via events. **[SPEC]** the first increment can ship **without** graph capture (correctness first); add capture as a measured optimization once DP+ZeRO-2 is green — it should mainly help the small-model/high-step-rate regime where launch overhead dominates.
196	- **Portability note** (`:134`): graph / hipGraph / XLA-compiled per backend; the capture is conceptually portable, the API is per-backend. H100-only this campaign.

198	### 2.7 Determinism across the decomposition (the A/A/A contract extends to N ranks)
199	The single-GPU kernel is A/A/A-clean by construction (ascending-CTA reductions, no float atomics — the whole `dispatch.py:805-833` saga). The decomposition adds **two** non-determinism surfaces:
200	1. **reduce-scatter / all-reduce float summation order across ranks.** NCCL's ring/tree reduction order is **not guaranteed bit-identical run-to-run** for floats. → for the **global scalars** (prodigy d, grokadamw norm, looksam ‖g‖) use **reduce-to-rank-0 + broadcast** with a fixed ascending-rank fp64 sum (mirrors the in-kernel CTA-0 ascending fp64 sum, `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc:545`). For the **grad reduce-scatter**, bf16/fp32 ring order differs but the *downstream optimizer* tolerates it within the existing parity tol **only if** every rank uses the SAME reduced grad — which reduce-scatter guarantees per-shard. **Cross-rank bit-determinism of the final params requires a fixed-order grad reduction** → see §6.4 (the cross-rank A/A/A gate) and the **fixed-order reduce** recommendation.
201	2. **shard boundary placement** must be deterministic (it is: `_even_partition` is pure, `distributed.py:717`).

206	
207	### 3.1 ZeRO-2 (state+grad shard, params resident) — fits the INTACT megakernel
208	- params replicated on every rank → **the fused kernel runs unchanged** (it reads full params, produces full local grad).
209	- grad: reduce-scatter over DP (each rank keeps its shard).
210	- opt state (m/v/...): each rank allocates only its `1/DP` shard.
211	- params after step: **no all-gather needed** (params are replicated; each rank updated only its shard, so a **`all_gather` of the updated param shards** IS needed to re-replicate — wait: ZeRO-2 keeps params replicated but each rank only *computes* its shard's update, so it must all-gather the updated params too). **Correction:** ZeRO-2 shards *grad + opt-state* but **not params**; to keep params replicated after a sharded update, you all-gather the updated param slices. The only ZeRO-2 vs ZeRO-3 difference is **whether params are sharded in HBM between steps** (ZeRO-3) or replicated (ZeRO-2). For our megakernel both still do the reduce-scatter(grad) + sharded-opt + all-gather(params) dance; **ZeRO-2's win is smaller (only m/v/grad sharded), ZeRO-3 adds the param-resident shard.**
212	- **This is a BRING-UP CHECKPOINT, not a candidate end state** (deliverable = full 4D+ZeRO-3, locked): ZeRO-2 = the SAME ZeRO-3 code path with param-sharding off (params resident), booted first because the kernel body is untouched — only the host-side reduce-scatter/all-gather + sharded-opt kernel are new. A failure here is attributable to the collective dance, not param residency; ALL of this code carries into ZeRO-3 unchanged. The flagship ships ZeRO-3.
213	
214	### 3.2 ZeRO-3 (param shard → per-layer all-gather) — the honest options
215	ZeRO-3 keeps only `1/DP` of params resident, so the fwd+bwd must **gather params on use**. The megakernel reads params throughout P1 (all layers, barrier-free) — so the gather granularity question is real:
216	
217	- **(a) Full pre-gather before launch.** All-gather the entire param set into a full `params[total]` buffer, run the intact kernel, free the buffer after. **No memory win** (you reconstitute the full param set in HBM for the kernel's lifetime) — defeats ZeRO-3's purpose. **Reject** as the steady-state, but it is the **trivially-correct fallback** and the **first ZeRO-3 increment** (proves reduce-scatter/all-gather + sharded-opt correctness with the kernel literally unchanged; memory win deferred).
218	- **(b) Per-phase gather between barrier phases.** Gather layer-`L`'s params just before P1 needs them, free after. **Problem:** P1 is **barrier-free within a tile across ALL layers** (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:22-24` explicitly rejects per-layer grid barriers — the whole tile flows through all layers with no barrier). There is **no per-layer seam** in P1 to hang a host-side gather on without reintroducing the rejected barrier. → **(b) is incompatible with the current fused fwd+bwd unless P1 is re-cut per-layer**, which sacrifices the barrier-free fusion (the asset). **Reject for the transformer megakernel** at small layer counts; **[SPEC]** could be viable at the 24-48-layer ladder depths where per-layer-block prefetch amortizes, but only if PP-style stage cuts already exist (§4).
219	- **(c) In-kernel NVSHMEM gather.** The kernel issues device-initiated `nvshmem_get` for a remote param shard exactly when a wgmma loop needs it (overlapping the get with compute on the resident shard). **[FRONTIER]** This is the same device-initiated-NVSHMEM machinery as TP (§5) and carries the same risk. It's the only option that gets ZeRO-3's memory win **without** cutting P1's barrier-free fusion.
220	
221	**Recommended increment path for ZeRO-3:**
222	1. **(a) full pre-gather** — ship it first. Correct, simple, validates the collective dance. Memory win = 0 but it unblocks PP/TP development and the science runs at sizes that fit anyway.
223	2. Measure: does any **target-scale** model (the 20-30B ceiling, `:132`) actually OOM with full-pre-gather ZeRO-3? At ≤13B single-node it likely **fits without the memory win** (the owner's own dissent, `:138`, notes DP+ZeRO-3 fits ≤6.7B on 8×80GB). If it fits, **(a) is sufficient** and (c) is unnecessary complexity.
224	3. Only if a target size OOMs under (a): pursue **(c) in-kernel NVSHMEM param gather**, co-developed with TP's NVSHMEM (§5), behind the same go/no-go gate. **Do NOT build (c) speculatively** — it's frontier risk for a memory win that may not be needed at single-node scale.

226	### 3.3 The honest ZeRO-3 memory accounting [SPEC]
227	At d=2048/25.4M params the model is tiny; ZeRO is irrelevant. ZeRO earns its keep at the flagship (`#14`/PARALLELISM-FINAL targets 6.7B→20-30B). For a 6.7B lean cell (adamw, ~18 B/param state per `:101`): params 27 GB fp32 + m/v 54 GB = 81 GB → **OOMs one 80 GB H100 by itself**; ZeRO-3 over 8 → ~10 GB/rank state, fits with room for activations+batch. For a 6.7B **heavy** cell (SG2 ~44 B/param, `:101`): state alone ~295 GB → ZeRO-3/8 ~37 GB/rank — fits. **So ZeRO-3 is genuinely required at the flagship size; option (a) full-pre-gather reconstitutes 27 GB of params transiently per step — that's the one number to watch for the OOM that forces option (c).**

241	## 4. Pipeline parallelism (PP)
242	
243	### 4.1 Where the megakernel could cut into stages
244	PP splits the **layer stack** across stages. The decoder megakernel runs all `kLayers` layers inside one P1 (barrier-free per tile). To make stage `s` own layers `[L_s, L_{s+1})`:
245	- **The cut is between layer blocks.** Unlike ZeRO-3's per-phase gather (§3.2(b), rejected), a PP cut is **coarser**: stage `s`'s kernel runs fwd for its layers, **sends activations** to stage `s+1` (host-NCCL P2P or NVSHMEM), which runs the next layers. The bwd reverses. Each stage is **its own megakernel launch** over its layer subset.
246	- **Crucially, PP breaks the fwd+bwd fusion** (`:138` foresaw this): a pipeline interleaves micro-batches' fwd and bwd (1F1B), so a stage's kernel can no longer do fwd-then-bwd-in-one-launch for a micro-batch — it does **fwd-only** launches and **bwd-only** launches, scheduled by the 1F1B driver. → **PP requires splitting the fused megakernel into a fwd-only and a bwd-only kernel** (the activations checkpoint to HBM, which the TC path **already does** via `DecActs`, `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:180` — the acts are already in HBM, so a fwd-only kernel that stops after writing `DecActs` + a bwd-only kernel that reads them is a **natural cut the current acts-to-HBM design enables**).
247	- **Per-layer-block boundaries already separated by grid barriers?** **No** — P1 is barrier-free across layers by design. PP's cut is therefore **per-launch** (one kernel per stage's layers), not per-in-kernel-barrier. The acts-to-HBM design (every layer's `X_in/X_ctx/X_x1/X_gact/dY_*` already staged to HBM) makes the stage boundary clean: stage `s+1` reads stage `s`'s `X_in[L_s]` from HBM (locally or via P2P).
248	
249	### 4.2 Microbatch scheduling (1F1B)
250	Standard 1F1B (Megatron). The `DistributedContext.pp_group` + `is_pipeline_first_stage`/`is_pipeline_last_stage` (`distributed.py:527`) already exist; the **schedule driver is new** (Python, host-side): warmup fwds, steady 1F1B, cooldown bwds, with `pp_group` P2P sends. This is **conventional** — the novelty/risk is entirely in splitting the fused kernel into fwd-only/bwd-only halves (§4.1).
251	
252	### 4.3 Honest cost analysis at race scale vs ladder depths
253	- **At 4-17 seq / 2-layer race models:** PP is **pure overhead** — 2 layers can't fill a 2+ stage pipeline (the bubble is the whole thing), and the activation send dominates the tiny compute. **PP buys nothing below ~GPT2-medium depth.** Do **not** PP the science/race runs.
254	- **At ladder depths (24-48 layers, the flagship):** PP becomes worthwhile **only when** the model doesn't fit even under TP+ZeRO-3, i.e. at the 20-30B ceiling (`:132`). The bubble fraction ≈ `(PP-1)/(microbatches + PP-1)`; at 48 layers / PP=2-4 with enough micro-batches it's amortizable. **[SPEC]** at ≤13B single-node, the owner's own dissent (`:138`) is correct that DP+ZeRO-3 likely beats anything with PP on throughput; PP's payoff is the multi-node / absolute-ceiling regime.
255	- **Verdict (owner-locked):** PP is the **3rd bring-up increment** (after ZeRO-3) and **SHIPS in the flagship regardless** — full 4D (DP×TP×PP) is the locked deliverable. The measurement plan still quantifies PP's per-size contribution honestly (expected: pure overhead at race scale; amortizing at 24-48-layer ladder depths; load-bearing at the 20-30B ceiling) and reports the measured crossover — but PP's inclusion in the flagship config is NOT contingent on the number.

259	## 5. Tensor parallelism via device-initiated NVSHMEM (the FRONTIER piece — LAST increment, explicit go/no-go)
260	
261	### 5.1 Where the all-reduce lands (Megatron col/row split)
262	TP splits each linear's weight matrix across `kTP` ranks. Megatron pattern for the decoder block:
263	- **Attention:** `in_proj` (QKV) is **column-parallel** (each rank owns `3d/TP` output cols → its own heads), `out_proj` is **row-parallel** (each rank owns `d/TP` input rows). The **all-reduce lands after `out_proj`** (sum the partial attention outputs across TP) — i.e. right where the current kernel finishes the attention block and adds the residual.
264	- **FFN:** `ff0` (d→dff) column-parallel, `ff2` (dff→d) row-parallel. **All-reduce after `ff2`**, before the residual add.
265	- So **two all-reduces per layer** (post-attn, post-FFN), exactly Megatron. In the megakernel these land in `dectc_forward_tile` after the `out_proj` GEMM (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:712`) and after the `ff2` GEMM (`:743`); the **backward** mirrors with all-reduces on the input-grad (dX) of the column-parallel pieces.
266	
267	### 5.2 Device-initiated NVSHMEM inside the wgmma loops
268	The owner locked **device-initiated NVSHMEM** to keep the fusion (`/workspace/.campaign_plan.md:131`): instead of ending the kernel to do a host-NCCL all-reduce, the kernel itself issues `nvshmemx_float_sum_reduce` (or a hand-rolled `nvshmem_put` + barrier ring) at the two reduce points, **inside the persistent kernel**, between the GridBarrier phases.
269	- The all-reduce sits on a **new in-kernel grid barrier** boundary: after the row-parallel GEMM writes its partial, `bar.sync()` → NVSHMEM all-reduce the partial across the `tp_group` → `bar.sync()` → continue. The GridBarrier substrate (`megakernel_common.cuh`) already gives the cross-CTA rendezvous; NVSHMEM gives the cross-**GPU** rendezvous.
270	- **Determinism (A/A/A) implication:** the cross-rank reduce **must be fixed-order**. A naive `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` does not guarantee a fixed float summation order across ranks → ULP drift run-to-run → A/A/A failure (the exact class the in-kernel ascending-CTA fix cured locally, `dispatch.py:805`). → **implement a fixed-order ring reduce** (rank 0 += rank 1 += ... ascending, fp32 or fp64 accumulate) so the order is structural, not timing-dependent. This is the cross-rank analogue of `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc`'s ascending-CTA fp64 sum (`:545`). **This is non-negotiable for the A/A/A gate (§6.4).**
271	
272	### 5.3 The host-NCCL fallback (if device-TP proves infeasible)
273	If device-initiated NVSHMEM TP can't hit parity/determinism/perf, **fall back to host-NCCL TP with the kernel split per-block**: cut the megakernel at the two reduce points into 3 sub-launches (pre-attn-reduce, attn-out→pre-ffn-reduce, post-ffn-reduce→end), host-NCCL `all_reduce` (the existing `DistributedContext.all_reduce_tp`, `distributed.py:536`, **already implemented**) between sub-launches. **This sacrifices the in-block fusion** (the whole point of device-TP) but is **conventional and low-risk** — it's literally Megatron with the megakernel as the per-block compute. The fallback is **always available** because `all_reduce_tp` already exists.
274	
275	### 5.4 Scope it as the LAST increment with an explicit go/no-go gate
276	**Build order (locked, `:139`):** DP+ZeRO-2 → ZeRO-3 → PP → **TP(NVSHMEM) last**.
277	**Go/no-go gate for device-TP (author this as `tests/hw/test_tp_nvshmem_gate.py`):**
278	- **GO criteria (all must hold):** (1) device-TP all-reduce produces **bit-identical** params to host-NCCL TP on the same input (parity); (2) **A/A/A bit-exact** across 3 re-runs (the fixed-order ring works); (3) device-TP MFU **beats** host-NCCL-split TP at the target TP degree (else there's no reason to take the frontier risk — just use the fallback); (4) it **composes** with ZeRO-3 + DP without deadlock (NVSHMEM + NCCL + GridBarrier coexistence).
279	- **NO-GO:** ship the **host-NCCL TP fallback** (§5.3) and record device-TP as future work. The flagship still gets 4D (DP×TP×PP+ZeRO-3) — just with host-NCCL TP instead of in-kernel NVSHMEM TP. **The owner's "maximal accomplishment" goal is met either way; only the in-block-fusion bragging right is at stake.**
280	- **Honest risk register [FRONTIER]:** NVSHMEM device-init comm inside a persistent megakernel with a hand-built GridBarrier is genuinely unproven in this codebase (zero existing NVSHMEM usage — grep confirms). Risks: (a) NVSHMEM init/teardown vs the persistent-kernel + CUDA-graph lifetime; (b) NVSHMEM barrier vs the custom GridBarrier interaction (two barrier systems must not deadlock); (c) register/occupancy pressure (the TC kernel is already at 128-166 regs decoder / **255 regs occ-1 zero-margin on mamba/vit**, `:152` — NVSHMEM calls may spill and **kill occupancy → GridBarrier hang**, the launcher's `occ>=1` refuse-or-hang invariant, `:291`); (d) determinism (§5.2). **Recommendation: this is the one piece most likely to slip or get descoped to the host-NCCL fallback. Plan the instance-hours so the flagship is shippable WITHOUT it (4D via host-NCCL TP), and treat in-kernel NVSHMEM TP as the stretch goal.**
281	
282	---
283	
284	## 6. NCCL/NVSHMEM bootstrap + Python orchestration deltas
285	
286	### 6.1 Bootstrap
287	- **NCCL:** via `torch.distributed` init — **already done** in `DistributedContext.initialize` (`distributed.py:331`, reads `WORLD_SIZE`/`RANK`, `init_process_group(backend="nccl")`, builds DP/TP/PP/EP subgroups). **Reuse as-is.**
288	- **NVSHMEM [FRONTIER]:** needs a separate `nvshmem_init` keyed to the same rank/world (bootstrapped off the NCCL uniqueId or MPI). New `csrc/bindings/nvshmem_bootstrap.cu` (host) exposed via a pybind `init_nvshmem(rank, world, tp_group_ranks)` called once per process after `init_process_group`, **only when `kTP>1` and the device-TP go-gate passed**. Teardown coordinated with CUDA-graph destroy. **This is new and is the riskiest bootstrap piece.**
289	
290	### 6.2 `fused_train_step` → a rank-aware variant
291	New `fused_train_step_distributed(..., par_ctx: DistributedContext, sharder: ZeRO3Sharder, par_config)` in `dispatch.py`, wrapping the existing `fused_train_step` (`:1714`):
292	```
293	1. (ZeRO-3) all_gather_params -> full `flat`         [sharder.all_gather_params, exists]
294	2. pack params -> flat; pack THIS RANK's batch shard inputs   [existing pack code]
295	3. ops.fused_step(..., opt_only=(ZeRO>=2 ? "stop-at-B2" : False), gemm_impl, par_point)
296	      -> local grad in grad_out[total]               [the kernel early-exits at B2 under ZeRO>=2, §2.2]
297	4. (global-scalar opts) all_reduce the prodigy/grokadamw/looksam scalar(s)  [fixed-order, §2.4]
298	5. reduce_scatter_grads(grad_out) -> owned grad shard [sharder.reduce_scatter_grads, exists]
299	6. sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> over the owned shard [new, §2.3]   (or in-kernel P3 if ZeRO<=1)
300	7. all_gather_params(updated shards) -> full params   [sharder.all_gather_params, exists]
301	8. scatter flat -> p.data; read loss                  [existing]
302	```
303	Steps 3-7 are the **CUDA-graph-captured** unit (§2.6). Steps 2/8 (host pack/scatter) are outside the graph.
304	- **The race driver (`grokking_race_v2.py` / the science loop) gets a `par_ctx` argument**; single-GPU runs pass a degenerate `world_size=1` context (every collective no-ops — `distributed.py` already guarantees this), so **the single-GPU path is literally unchanged** (the no-op-collective degradation is the same property that keeps imports safe today).
305	- **Launcher:** `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8` (reuse `test_3d_parallel.py`'s `__main__` pattern, `:312`). A custom launcher is **not needed** — torchrun + the existing env-var bootstrap suffices. **[SPEC]** NVSHMEM may want MPI launch instead of torchrun; if so, a thin `mpirun` wrapper that also sets the torch env vars (so both NCCL and NVSHMEM bootstrap) — decide at the device-TP go-gate, not before.
306	
307	### 6.3 wiring_check / tail-gate / A-A-A extended to N ranks
308	- `wiring_check.py` (the arbiter, asserts path==L3-TC via captured `LAST_L3_ENGINE=="wgmma"`, `wiring_check.py:14`) gains a **rank-aware mode**: under a launched job, **every rank** must report `engine=="wgmma"` and pass its **local** tail-gate; rank 0 aggregates. The per-rank check is the existing check; the new part is the **collective assertion that all ranks agree** (a `dist.all_reduce` of a pass/fail bit, fail-loud if any rank diverges).
309	- The tail-gate parity (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py`) runs **per-rank on its shard** vs a single-GPU oracle restricted to that shard — the sharded-opt kernel must match the in-kernel P3 over the same elements (§7.3).
310	
311	### 6.4 THE cross-rank bit-determinism gate (new, the load-bearing multi-GPU correctness check)
312	New `tests/hw/test_cross_rank_determinism.py`: run the **same** init + data on `N` ranks, A/A/A (3 re-runs), assert the **final all-gathered params are bit-identical across all 3 runs AND match the single-GPU reference within the existing parity tol** (SG-family ~3e-5 fp32, per `/workspace/.campaign_plan.md:12`). This is the gate that forces:
313	- fixed-order grad reduction (reduce-to-rank-0+broadcast for scalars; a fixed-order/tree reduce-scatter for grad, §2.7);
314	- fixed-order NVSHMEM ring for TP (§5.2);
315	- deterministic shard boundaries (already true).
316	**Without this gate the multi-GPU path is not trustworthy** — it is the N-rank extension of the A/A/A discipline that the entire single-GPU campaign already lives by. **This is the single most important new test.**
317	
318	---
319	
320	## 7. What is single-GPU-unit-testable NOW (author + test before the 8×H100 window)
321	
322	This section is the whole point of doing the design first: **maximize what's authored and validated on 1 GPU so the rental window is short.** The owner provisions 8×H100 *later*; everything below can be built and gated on the current single H100.
323	
324	### 7.1 Single-rank NCCL loopback correctness of the decomposition
325	- `torchrun --nproc_per_node=1` (or even CPU `gloo`) exercises the **full** `fused_train_step_distributed` control flow with `world_size=1`: reduce-scatter/all-gather become identity (each rank owns everything), the sharded-opt kernel runs over the whole param set, and the result must **equal the in-kernel-P3 single-GPU path bit-for-bit** (the degenerate-collective specialization, `distributed.py` no-ops). **This validates the entire host orchestration + the sharded-opt-kernel-vs-fused-P3 equivalence with ZERO multi-GPU hardware.** The existing `test_3d_parallel.py` CPU tests (`:240-273`) already prove the mesh/shard math offline — extend them to drive the real (loopback) kernel step.
326	- **Multi-rank loopback on 1 GPU:** torchrun `--nproc_per_node=2` with both ranks on `cuda:0` (NCCL supports this) gives a **real 2-rank reduce-scatter/all-gather** sharing one GPU — validates the **collective wiring + cross-rank determinism gate (§6.4) at DP=2** without a second GPU. **[SPEC]** NCCL multi-rank-one-GPU works for correctness (not perf); confirms the shard partition + fixed-order reduce before the 8-GPU window.
327	
328	### 7.2 Template-instantiation compile tests for all config points
329	The build instantiates a **fixed allow-list** of `ParConfig` points (the only ones `dispatch.cpp` can route to). New `tests/hw/test_parallel_instantiation.py` (CPU, `nvcc -c` only, no run): assert **every** allow-listed `<Opt, ParConfig<...>>` **compiles** (catches `if constexpr`/ABI breakage early). Allow-list (the campaign's real points):
330	```
331	<*, SingleGPU>                              -- the bit-identical baseline (PTX-diff gated, §1.2)
332	<*, ParConfig<8,1,1,1,Z2>>                  -- DP8 + ZeRO-2  (increment 1)
333	<*, ParConfig<8,1,1,1,Z3>>                  -- DP8 + ZeRO-3  (increment 2)
334	<*, ParConfig<4,1,2,1,Z3>>                  -- + PP2         (increment 3)
335	<*, ParConfig<2,4,1,1,Z3>>, <*, ParConfig<1,4,2,1,Z3>>  -- + TP4 (increment 4, frontier)
336	```
337	Compiling all of these on 1 GPU (or just `nvcc -c`) **front-loads every template/ABI bug** before the rental window. **This is the cheapest, highest-leverage pre-work.**
338	
339	### 7.3 The sharded-optimizer kernel vs the fused tail at DP=1
340	New `tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py`: at DP=1, `sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt>` over the full param set must produce **bit-identical** params to the in-kernel P3 (`apply_optimizer<Opt>` work-steal loop) on the same `(params, grad, state)`. Run for **all 11 OptIds** (elementwise trivially; muon/SG11/SG15/SG2 with the tensor-granular shard = whole model on rank 0, so their P2.x stages run intact). **This proves the cut at B2 (§2.2) is correctness-preserving per optimizer — fully on 1 GPU.**
341	
342	### 7.4 Graph-capture of the decomposed step on 1 GPU
343	New `tests/hw/test_step_graph_capture.py`: capture the `[kernel → (loopback) reduce-scatter → sharded-opt → (loopback) all-gather]` sequence as a CUDA graph on 1 GPU, replay `N` times, assert each replay equals the eager (non-graphed) step bit-for-bit and the loss trajectory matches a non-graphed run. **Validates the graph boundary + persistent-buffer addressing (§2.6) before multi-GPU**, where graph bugs are far costlier to debug.
344	
345	### 7.5 What genuinely CANNOT be tested on 1 GPU (the irreducible 8×H100 work)
346	Be honest: these need the real hardware window —
347	- **NVSHMEM device-init TP** (no loopback for device-initiated cross-GPU comm; needs ≥2 real GPUs with NVLink). The go/no-go gate (§5.4) is an 8-GPU activity.
348	- **Weak-scaling efficiency** (the ≥70% bar, `test_3d_parallel.py:143`) — needs real 1→8 scaling.
349	- **PP bubble / 1F1B throughput** at real stage counts.
350	- **Cross-node** anything (out of scope this campaign — single-node 8×H100).
351	Everything **else** (orchestration, sharded-opt correctness, template instantiation, graph capture, the determinism gate at DP=2-loopback) is **1-GPU-authorable now.** **Target: walk into the 8-GPU window with only NVSHMEM-TP + scaling-measurement left.**
352	
353	---
354	
355	## 8. Measurement plan + kill-gates per increment (tied to instance-hours)
356	
357	**Discipline (owner-clarified 2026-06-12):** increments are the **bring-up order of ONE system whose locked end state is full 4D+ZeRO-3** — every dimension ships in the flagship. Each increment has a **bring-up gate** (what must be green to call that layer validated and move on) and a **measurement** (that dimension's honest contribution, reported). **No gate demotes the flagship config.** The one implementation go/no-go is TP's mechanism (device-NVSHMEM vs host-NCCL — both ARE TP). Metric = **throughput (tokens/s)** and **per-GPU roofline %** (`roofline.py` bf16_tc=989.4e12). Target scale = the **flagship** (6.7B→ the 20-30B ceiling), NOT the race toy.
358	
359	| Increment | Bring-up gate (move on when green) | Measurement reported (not a descope trigger) | Instance-hour note |
360	|---|---|---|---|
361	| **0. SingleGPU `<Opt,SingleGPU>`** | PTX **bit-identical** to legacy `<Opt>` (§1.2) | — | **CPU/1-GPU, ~free.** Gate before anything else. |
362	| **1. DP8 + ZeRO-2** (= Z3 code, param-shard off) | collectives + sharded-opt + cross-rank A/A/A green (§6.4); DP weak-scaling measured | DP scaling efficiency 1→8 | First multi-GPU spend. **Short:** orchestration pre-validated on 1 GPU (§7) — a measurement session, not a debug session. |
363	| **2. ZeRO-3 ON** | param-shard residency green at equal correctness; OOM-threshold measured (§3.3) | max-fit size vs ZeRO-2; throughput delta; whether option (c) NVSHMEM-gather is ever needed | The flagship runs Z3 regardless; the measurement informs the gather-option choice, not the stage. |
364	| **3. + PP** | fwd/bwd-split kernels + 1F1B driver green at flagship depth | PP's contribution per size (bubble cost at ≤13B vs payoff at the ceiling) — the measured crossover | PP ships in the flagship (locked); enable the measured-best degree per size. |
365	| **4. + TP** | the §5.4 go/no-go decides the MECHANISM: device-NVSHMEM (stretch) vs host-NCCL (fallback). Either way TP ships. | device-vs-host TP MFU; TP's contribution at the flagship | **Highest-risk spend** — budget so the flagship lands as 4D-with-host-NCCL-TP even if NVSHMEM slips. |
366	
367	**Cross-cutting:** the contribution analysis (which dimension bought what at which scale) is REPORTED as the measured finding — it's the honest-engineering layer of the portfolio — but the flagship config is **DP×TP×PP+ZeRO-3 at max batch, full stop.** Degrees per size are tuned (e.g. DP2×TP2×PP2 = 8 GPUs as the canonical all-dims-active point; pure-DP8 measured alongside as the comparison baseline). Instance-hours: bill for bring-up + measurement, not for re-litigating the locked decision (`:65-72`).
368	
369	**Tear-down signal (`:72`):** the moment the flagship is locked (4D-or-best-measured-subset + cross-rank A/A/A + weak-scaling reported), signal the owner to kill the instance.
370	
371	---
372	
373	## 9. Summary of new files / edits this design implies (the build manifest)
374	
375	**New C++/CUDA:**
376	- `csrc/fused/sm_90/parallel_config.cuh` — the `ParConfig` template + `SingleGPU` (§1).
377	- `csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh` — the post-reduce-scatter sharded opt (§2.3).
378	- `csrc/bindings/nvshmem_bootstrap.cu` — **[FRONTIER]**, only on device-TP GO (§6.1).
379	- edits to `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` (+ vit/mamba twins): add `class Par` param, `if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad) return;` after B2 (§2.2), `if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)` NVSHMEM reduces in `dectc_forward_tile`/`backward` (§5.2). **All gated so `SingleGPU` is byte-identical.**
380	- edits to `dispatch.cpp` — route `(dp,tp,pp,zero)` → explicit `ParConfig` instantiation (§1.3, §7.2).
381	
382	**Python (mostly EXTEND the existing layer):**
383	- `distributed.py` — add `sequence_parallel` field; add `partition_tensor_granular` (§3.4); map `ParallelConfig` → C++ `ParConfig` point.
384	- `dispatch.py` — `fused_train_step_distributed` (§6.2); rank-aware `fused_step` plumbing of the par point + stop-at-B2 flag.
385	- `megakernel_engine.py` — reuse as-is (the framework adapter still works; the new path is the lower-level one).
386	
387	**New tests (ALL 1-GPU/CPU-authorable except the last two):**
388	- `test_parallel_identity.py` (§1.2, PTX diff), `test_parallel_instantiation.py` (§7.2), `test_sharded_optimizer.py` (§7.3), `test_step_graph_capture.py` (§7.4), `test_cross_rank_determinism.py` (§6.4, DP=2 loopback on 1 GPU then real on 8), rank-aware `wiring_check.py` mode (§6.3).
389	- **8-GPU only:** `test_tp_nvshmem_gate.py` (§5.4), weak-scaling via the existing `test_3d_parallel.py` harness (§7.5).
390	
391	**Reuse unchanged:** the GridBarrier substrate (`megakernel_common.cuh`), the acts-to-HBM `DecActs` design (it's what makes PP's fwd/bwd split clean, §4.1), `ZeRO3Sharder.reduce_scatter_grads`/`all_gather_params` (`distributed.py`), the Megatron rank mesh, the DeepSpeed config emitter.
392	
393	---
394	
395	## 10. The honest bottom line (risks + the contract)
396	
397	- **Lowest risk, do first:** the `SingleGPU` byte-identity gate (§1.2) + DP+ZeRO-2 (§3.1) + the entire 1-GPU-testable suite (§7). This is ~all authorable before the rental window and de-risks the orchestration + the B2 cut + per-optimizer sharding.
398	- **Medium risk:** ZeRO-3 option (a) (§3.2) — correct but may not deliver the memory win without option (c); PP (§4) — conventional machinery, ships in the flagship; its per-size contribution is a reported measurement.
399	- **Highest risk [FRONTIER]:** device-initiated NVSHMEM TP (§5) — unproven in this codebase, register/occupancy + determinism + NVSHMEM-vs-GridBarrier-vs-CUDAgraph interactions. **Budget so the flagship ships as 4D-via-host-NCCL-TP without it; treat in-kernel NVSHMEM as the stretch.**
400	- **The one non-negotiable:** the cross-rank A/A/A determinism gate (§6.4) and its fixed-order reductions (§2.7, §5.2). The entire single-GPU campaign is built on A/A/A; the multi-GPU path is not trustworthy until it extends to N ranks.
401	- **The structural win we got for free:** the existing **acts-to-HBM** design and the **persistent state_cache** mean (a) PP's fwd/bwd split is a natural cut, and (b) the step is CUDA-graph-capturable with no buffer-lifetime redesign. The B2 `sync_reset` seam is *already* the exact "after the grad reduce-scatter" cut the owner specified.
402	
403	This is the Phase-2 contract. Execute increments 0-1 + the 1-GPU test suite before provisioning; walk into the 8×H100 window with only NVSHMEM-TP and the scaling measurements left.

5	// (the metaprogrammed template the L3-TC megakernel is specialized over).
6	//
7	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §1.1 (the ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,
8	// SP,ZeROStage> struct + the SingleGPU alias) and §1.2 (the bit-identical
9	// single-GPU contract — the kEmitComm gate that makes every comm branch fold
10	// away to ZERO code when the config is degenerate).
11	//
12	// HEADER-ONLY, SELF-CONTAINED, device+host. Included by every megakernel TU
13	// (decoder/vit/mamba) so the SAME translation unit can hold BOTH the single-GPU
14	// point AND a multi-GPU flagship point in one fat binary (design §1.2 — the
15	// discriminator is a TEMPLATE PARAMETER, not a TU-wide macro, because the
16	// campaign ships the single-GPU artifact alongside the 4D+ZeRO-3 flagship).
17	//
18	// WHY constexpr-everything: ALL fields are `static constexpr`, so every branch
19	// that reads them (`if constexpr (Par::kEmitComm)`, `if constexpr (Par::
20	// kShardOptGrad)`, …) folds at compile time. For the degenerate SingleGPU point
21	// the compiler emits NO NVSHMEM symbols, NO extra barriers, NO `comm` reads ⇒
22	// `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, SingleGPU>` is byte-for-byte identical to
23	// today's `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (design §1.2, the PTX-diff gate).
24	//
25	// THIS FILE ADDS NO MATH AND NO COMM. It is the pure compile-time config carrier
26	// + an empty CommCtx POD (the megakernel's default `comm` argument; populated
27	// with NCCL/NVSHMEM handles ONLY on the kEmitComm path, which a kernel builder
28	// wires later — out of scope here). Authored 1-GPU/CPU per design §7.
29	// ============================================================================
30	
31	#include <cstdint>
32	
33	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace par {
34	
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	//  ZeRO stage (design §1.1). Z0=none, Z1=opt-state shard, Z2=+grad shard,
37	//  Z3=+param shard. The flagship ships Z3 (design DELIVERABLE line); Z2 is the
38	//  SAME code path with param-sharding off (a stage flag), the first bring-up
39	//  increment (design §3.1).
40	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	enum class ZeROStage : int { Z0 = 0, Z1 = 1, Z2 = 2, Z3 = 3 };
42	
43	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	//  ParConfig — the compile-time 4D(+ZeRO) parallelism point (design §1.1).
45	//
46	//  The (DP, TP, PP, SP, ZeRO) tuple maps 1:1 to the Python-side ParallelConfig
47	//  (distributed.py) per design §1.3. ALL fields constexpr ⇒ every consumer
48	//  branch folds; the degenerate point emits zero comm code (design §1.2).
49	//
50	//  SP (sequence-parallel) is EXPRESSIBLE but pinned to 1 this campaign: at the
51	//  race's seq 4-17 a sequence split is moot (design §1.1 / PARALLELISM-FINAL),
52	//  so the static_assert below makes any SP!=1 instantiation a loud BUILD error
53	//  rather than a silently-broken path.
54	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
55	template <int DP, int TP, int PP, int SP, ZeROStage Z>
56	struct ParConfig {
57	    static constexpr int        kDP   = DP;   // data-parallel replicas
58	    static constexpr int        kTP   = TP;   // tensor-parallel ranks (Megatron col/row split)
59	    static constexpr int        kPP   = PP;   // pipeline stages
60	    static constexpr int        kSP   = SP;   // sequence-parallel (kept EXPRESSIBLE, fixed 1)
61	    static constexpr ZeROStage  kZeRO = Z;
62	
63	    // ── Derived compile-time gates (design §1.1). These are the predicates the
64	    //    megakernel + sharded-opt kernel branch on with `if constexpr`. ────────
65	    static constexpr bool kIsSingleGPU = (DP == 1 && TP == 1 && PP == 1 && SP == 1);
66	    static constexpr bool kEmitComm     = !kIsSingleGPU;        // gate ALL NVSHMEM/NCCL
67	    static constexpr bool kShardParams  = (Z == ZeROStage::Z3);  // ZeRO-3 param residency shard
68	    static constexpr bool kShardOptGrad = (Z >= ZeROStage::Z2);  // ZeRO>=2 grad+opt-state shard
69	                                                                 // ⇒ kernel early-exits at B2 (§2.2)
70	    static constexpr bool kTPComm       = (TP > 1);             // in-kernel TP all-reduce (§5)
71	    static constexpr bool kPPStage      = (PP > 1);             // pipeline stage cut (§4)
72	
73	    // SP is expressible but must be 1 this campaign (design §1.1 static_assert).
74	    static_assert(SP == 1, "SP axis is expressible but must be 1 this campaign "
75	                           "(seq 4-17 makes a seq split moot; #14 / PARALLELISM-FINAL).");
76	    static_assert(DP >= 1 && TP >= 1 && PP >= 1 && SP >= 1, "degrees must be >= 1");
77	};
78	
79	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80	//  THE single-GPU guarantee, named once so the static_asserts read cleanly
81	//  (design §1.1). `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, SingleGPU>` MUST be
82	//  byte-identical to the legacy `<Opt>` overload — enforced by kEmitComm==false
83	//  folding every comm branch away (design §1.2). This is the default template
84	//  arg of the megakernel, so existing call sites compile unchanged.
85	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86	using SingleGPU = ParConfig<1, 1, 1, 1, ZeROStage::Z0>;
87	
88	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
89	//  CommCtx — the megakernel's default trailing argument (design §1.1 kernel
90	//  signature: `par::CommCtx comm /* default-constructed, unused when
91	//  !kEmitComm */`). It is an EMPTY POD here on purpose:
92	//
93	//   * On the SingleGPU / kEmitComm==false path the kernel never reads it, so the
94	//     ABI of the `<Opt>`-only overload is preserved (the old non-Par launcher
95	//     forwards a default-constructed CommCtx) and the PTX is unchanged.
96	//   * On the kEmitComm==true path a kernel builder widens this POD with the
97	//     NVSHMEM team handle / NCCL comm / tp_group rank table / peer param-shard
98	//     base pointers the in-kernel collectives need (design §5.2/§6.1). That
99	//     widening is GPU-window work and is intentionally NOT authored here (this
100	//     file is 1-GPU/CPU pre-work per design §7); the empty struct is the stable
101	//     seam those fields hang off without touching any single-GPU call site.
102	//
103	//  Trivially constructible/copyable so it is a valid by-value kernel parameter
104	//  and a no-cost default argument.
105	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
106	struct CommCtx {
107	    // rank within the world / the per-axis groups (filled only when kEmitComm).
108	    // Defaults describe the degenerate single-GPU world so a default-constructed
109	    // CommCtx is the correct "no comm" value the single-GPU path forwards.
110	    int world_size = 1;
111	    int world_rank = 0;
112	    int dp_size = 1, dp_rank = 0;
113	    int tp_size = 1, tp_rank = 0;
114	    int pp_size = 1, pp_rank = 0;
115	    // Opaque handle slots (NVSHMEM team / NCCL comm) — left as nullptr-able
116	    // pointers a builder casts to the concrete handle type behind kEmitComm, so
117	    // this header need NOT include <nccl.h>/<nvshmem.h> (kept CPU-compilable).
118	    void* tp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm / NVSHMEM team for the TP group (§5)
119	    void* dp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm for the DP group (reduce-scatter / all-gather)
120	};
121	
122	}}}  // namespace sg::fused::par
123	
124	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_PARALLEL_CONFIG_CUH_

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_SHARDED_OPTIMIZER_KERNEL_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_SHARDED_OPTIMIZER_KERNEL_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh — the POST-reduce-scatter
5	// sharded optimizer kernel for the ZeRO-2/3 multi-GPU step.
6	//
7	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §2.3 (the new, small sharded-
8	// optimizer kernel) — the second half of the owner's B2-seam decomposition
9	// (design §0.1/§2.1):
10	//     [fwd+bwd megakernel] → reduce-scatter(grad) → [THIS kernel] → all-gather(params)
11	//
12	// WHAT IT IS: under ZeRO>=2 the fused megakernel early-exits right after the B2
13	// barrier (design §2.2, `if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad) return;`) with the
14	// reduced LOCAL grad assembled. The host then reduce-scatters that grad so each
15	// rank holds the reduced grad for ONLY its owned shard. THIS kernel applies the
16	// optimizer over that owned shard. For the ELEMENTWISE optimizers it is exactly
17	// P3 (the fused tail) with the work-steal-over-30-tensors loop replaced by a
18	// flat grid-stride over [0, shard_numel) and NO GridBarrier (single phase).
19	//
20	// ZERO NEW MATH (design §2.3, the parity guarantee): every per-element update is
21	// the EXACT SAME `apply_optimizer<Opt>` from opt_components.cuh — the canonical
22	// `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` device math the in-kernel P3 tail already calls and
23	// the parity gates already validate. This file INCLUDES opt_components.cuh and
24	// reuses it verbatim; it does NOT edit it and adds no new optimizer math, so the
25	// sharded path inherits the single-GPU A/A/A correctness per element (design
26	// §7.3: the DP=1 sharded kernel must be bit-identical to the in-kernel P3).
27	//
28	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29	//  THE PER-TENSOR BOUNDARY (design §2.3 / §3.4 / §0.4) — read before using this
30	//  for muon / SuperGrok11 / SuperGrok15 / SuperGrok2:
31	//
32	//  `apply_optimizer<Opt>` is, for ALL 11 OptIds, a PURELY ELEMENTWISE update of
33	//  one `idx`: it consumes ONLY per-element state (exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema/...) and
34	//  PRE-COMPUTED inputs carried in FusedOptState (st.orth, st.mu, st.gate,
35	//  st.smart_grad, st.sam_dir, st.d_factor, st.clip_coef, ...). So this flat
36	//  grid-stride kernel COMPILES and RUNS correctly for any OptId *whose
37	//  FusedOptState inputs are already filled* — i.e. it is a complete, correct
38	//  optimizer step for:
39	//
40	//    ELEMENTWISE-DRIVABLE (this kernel alone is sufficient at DP):
41	//      adamw(0), lion(1), grokfast(2), neuralgrok(6),
42	//      and the ELEMENTWISE CORE of grokadamw(3)/looksam(4)/prodigy(5)
43	//      *given* their global/precomputed scalar already in st (clip_coef /
44	//      sam_dir / d_factor — see the next paragraph for where those come from).
45	//
46	//    PER-TENSOR / PER-MATRIX (this kernel is the APPLY ONLY — its st inputs need
47	//    an UPSTREAM stage that is OUT OF SCOPE for this kernel):
48	//      muon(7)        → st.orth     : Newton–Schulz over a WHOLE 2D weight (P2.7)
49	//      supergrok11(8) → st.mu/gate  : per-TENSOR meta-net mu/gate (P2.45)
50	//      supergrok15(9) → st.mu/gate  : per-TENSOR meta-net mu     (P2.45)
51	//      supergrok2(10) → st.smart_grad: per-TENSOR CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU + segmented
52	//                                      sort meta-net (STAGE -1 + P3-SG2)
53	//    Those P2.x stages cooperate across CTAs PER matrix/tensor on the GridBarrier
54	//    substrate, so they REQUIRE the tensor whole on one rank — which forces the
55	//    ZeRO-3 shard to be TENSOR-GRANULAR for these cells (design §3.4;
56	//    grokking_optimizers/parallel/shard_map.py::partition_tensor_granular). The
57	//    sharded-optimizer kernel FOR THEM is the *full* persistent megakernel
58	//    restricted to the tensors this rank owns (design §2.3) — NOT this flat
59	//    kernel. This flat kernel deliberately does NOT run those P2.x stages; it
60	//    only does the elementwise apply once their st inputs exist.
61	//
62	//  Likewise the GLOBAL-scalar cells (prodigy d, grokadamw grad-norm clip_coef,
63	//  looksam ‖g‖) need a cross-DP all-reduce of one/two scalars BEFORE this kernel
64	//  (design §2.4) so every rank's `st.d_factor`/`st.clip_coef` agree; that
65	//  all-reduce is host-side orchestration (design §6.2 step 4), also out of scope
66	//  here. This kernel just consumes the agreed scalar from st.
67	//
68	//  Net: every OptId COMPILE-CHECKS here (apply_optimizer is elementwise). Which
69	//  ones are *correct from this kernel alone* vs need the upstream stage/all-
70	//  reduce is the taxonomy above — documented per design §2.3/§3.4, enforced by
71	//  the host shard-mode selection (elementwise → flat-even; per-tensor →
72	//  tensor-granular).
73	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	//
75	// CPU/1-GPU AUTHORABLE (design §7.3): this is the cut the test_sharded_optimizer
76	// gate validates entirely on one GPU. Authored here as NEW code; the kernel
77	// builder owns wiring it into dispatch + the explicit instantiations.
78	// ============================================================================
79	
80	#include <cstdint>
81	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
82	
83	// The canonical per-optimizer elementwise math + the FusedOptState ABI. We REUSE
84	// apply_optimizer<Opt> / OptId / FusedOptState verbatim — INCLUDE, do not edit
85	// (design §2.3: zero new math, reuse the validated single-GPU tail).
86	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh"
87	
88	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
89	
90	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
91	//  sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt, Par> — flat grid-stride over the OWNED shard.
92	//
93	//  Args (design §2.3 signature):
94	//    params_shard : [shard_numel] this rank's owned param slice (mutated in place)
95	//    grad_shard   : [shard_numel] the reduce-scattered grad for the owned slice
96	//    lr, step     : the step's learning rate + 1-based step counter
97	//    st_shard     : FusedOptState whose pointers are ALREADY rebased to the shard
98	//                   (the host offsets exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema/... to the owned
99	//                   slice before launch — the per-element ABI is shard-local, so
100	//                   index `i` into params_shard pairs with index `i` into every
101	//                   st_shard buffer, exactly like the in-kernel P3 owns each
102	//                   element once). st_shard also carries the per-step scalars
103	//                   already folded via apply_scalars (bc1/bc2/d_factor/clip_coef/
104	//                   gate/...), and the precomputed per-tensor pointers (orth/mu/
105	//                   smart_grad/sam_dir) for the per-tensor cells.
106	//
107	//  NO GridBarrier (single phase): the work-steal-over-30-tensors loop of P3 is
108	//  replaced by one flat grid-stride over [0, shard_numel). Each element is
109	//  written exactly once by the thread that owns its `i`, so there is no cross-CTA
110	//  dependence and no barrier (design §2.3). `lr` is threaded into st_shard.lr so
111	//  apply_optimizer reads a single source for the rate (matches the P3 contract).
112	//
113	//  Par is carried for ABI/symmetry with the megakernel template (design §1.1)
114	//  and to let a builder add `if constexpr (Par::kEmitComm)` hooks later (e.g. a
115	//  fused all-gather-on-write for ZeRO-3). It is otherwise unused by the
116	//  elementwise apply — the shard is already local when this kernel runs.
117	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
118	template <OptId Opt, class Par>
119	__global__ void sharded_optimizer_kernel(
120	        float* __restrict__ params_shard,        // [shard_numel] owned param slice
121	        const float* __restrict__ grad_shard,    // [shard_numel] reduce-scattered grad
122	        int64_t shard_numel,
123	        float lr, int step,
124	        FusedOptState st_shard /* pointers pre-rebased to the shard */) {
125	    // Single source for the rate (the P3 tail reads st.lr; mirror that here so a
126	    // caller that passes lr positionally and a caller that pre-folds it via
127	    // apply_scalars agree bit-for-bit).
128	    st_shard.lr = lr;
129	
130	    const int64_t stride = static_cast<int64_t>(blockDim.x) * gridDim.x;
131	    int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
132	    for (; i < shard_numel; i += stride) {
133	        // EXACT same canonical math as the in-kernel P3 tail (opt_components.cuh).
134	        // Shard-local index i pairs params_shard[i] with grad_shard[i] and every
135	        // pre-rebased st_shard buffer at [i]. Zero new math (design §2.3).
136	        apply_optimizer<Opt>(params_shard, grad_shard, i, step, st_shard);
137	    }
138	}
139	
140	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
141	//  Host launcher — a thin grid-stride launch (design §2.3: "~30 lines, no
142	//  GridBarrier, single phase"). Sized to the shard, NOT the full param set. A
143	//  kernel builder routes this from dispatch behind the ZeRO>=2 path + the
144	//  explicit ParConfig instantiation allow-list (design §1.3/§7.2); it is left
145	//  here as the canonical small launcher so the kernel has a tested entry point.
146	//
147	//  NOTE: no GPU is launched in this CPU/1-GPU pre-work (design §7); this launcher
148	//  is COMPILE-CHECKED only. block=256 mirrors the per-op elementwise launchers'
149	//  default; grid is capped so the grid-stride covers any shard_numel.
150	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151	template <OptId Opt, class Par>
152	inline cudaError_t launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel(
153	        float* params_shard, const float* grad_shard, int64_t shard_numel,
154	        float lr, int step, const FusedOptState& st_shard,
155	        cudaStream_t stream = nullptr, int block = 256, int max_grid = 65535) {
156	    if (shard_numel <= 0) return cudaSuccess;
157	    int64_t want = (shard_numel + block - 1) / block;
158	    int grid = static_cast<int>(want < max_grid ? want : max_grid);
159	    if (grid < 1) grid = 1;
160	    sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt, Par><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
161	        params_shard, grad_shard, shard_numel, lr, step, st_shard);
162	    return cudaGetLastError();
163	}
164	
165	}}} // namespace sg::fused::sm90
166	
167	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_SHARDED_OPTIMIZER_KERNEL_CUH_
