1	"""grokking_optimizers/parallel/shard_map.py — the ZeRO shard PARTITION.
2	
3	IMPLEMENTS /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §3.4 (the shard partition that
4	respects the per-TENSOR optimizer constraint) + the elementwise even-partition
5	helper (design §2.4 "shard the flat [0,total) by even-partition").
6	
7	THE PROBLEM (design §3.4): ``ZeRO3Sharder._even_partition`` splits the FLAT param
8	buffer mid-tensor. That breaks muon / SuperGrok11 / SuperGrok15 / SuperGrok2 —
9	their P2.x optimizer stages (Newton–Schulz over a whole 2D weight; the per-tensor
10	meta-net mu/gate; SG2's segmented sort + CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU) need the WHOLE
11	matrix/tensor on ONE rank (design §0.4/§2.4). So the ZeRO-3 shard for those cells
12	must be TENSOR-GRANULAR, not element-granular.
13	
14	THIS MODULE (pure functions on SIZE LISTS — no torch, no torch.distributed, no
15	GPU, so it is CPU/CI-testable per design §7):
16	
17	  * :func:`even_partition`            — the flat element partition (mirrors
18	                                        ``distributed._even_partition`` exactly).
19	  * :func:`partition_elementwise_even`— per-rank flat slices for the ELEMENTWISE
20	                                        optimizers (finer, best balance).
21	  * :func:`partition_tensor_granular` — assign WHOLE tensors to ranks (greedy by
22	                                        numel, balanced) so NO tensor is split —
23	                                        REQUIRED for muon/SG11/SG15/SG2 (§3.4).
24	  * :func:`shard_mode_for_optimizer`  — key the mode off the optimizer (§3.4:
25	                                        elementwise → flat-even; per-tensor →
26	                                        tensor-granular).
27	
28	It does NOT touch ``distributed.py``; a caller (e.g. a future
29	``fused_train_step_distributed``, design §6.2) picks the mode via
30	:func:`shard_mode_for_optimizer` and calls the matching partitioner.
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import dataclasses
36	from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
37	
38	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
39	#  Optimizer → shard-mode taxonomy (design §0.4 / §2.4 / §3.4).
40	#
41	#  ELEMENTWISE: shard the flat [0,total) — every per-element update is local, so
42	#  splitting a tensor across ranks is fine. (grokadamw/looksam/prodigy are
43	#  elementwise at APPLY; their global scalar is handled by a tiny all-reduce, NOT
44	#  by the shard partition — so they shard elementwise here.)
45	#
46	#  PER-TENSOR: a whole matrix/tensor must live on one rank (the P2.x stage reads
47	#  the whole tensor cooperatively). muon is per-MATRIX (NS over each 2D weight);
48	#  SG11/SG15/SG2 are per-TENSOR (meta-net over each tensor's elements).
49	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50	ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS = frozenset({
51	    "adamw", "lion", "grokfast", "grokadamw", "looksam", "prodigy", "neuralgrok",
52	})
53	PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS = frozenset({
54	    "muon", "supergrok11", "supergrok15", "supergrok2",
55	})
56	
57	# OptId integers (mirror csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::OptId) so a caller
58	# holding the numeric id can map to a mode too. Single source of the spelling.
59	_OPTID_TO_NAME: Dict[int, str] = {
60	    0: "adamw", 1: "lion", 2: "grokfast", 3: "grokadamw", 4: "looksam",
61	    5: "prodigy", 6: "neuralgrok", 7: "muon", 8: "supergrok11",
62	    9: "supergrok15", 10: "supergrok2",
63	}
64	
65	_MODE_ELEMENTWISE = "elementwise_even"
66	_MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR = "tensor_granular"
67	
68	
69	def shard_mode_for_optimizer(opt) -> str:
70	    """Return the shard mode an optimizer requires (design §3.4).
71	
72	    ``opt`` may be the optimizer NAME (str, case-insensitive) or its OptId int
73	    (0..10). Per-tensor cells (muon/SG11/SG15/SG2) → ``"tensor_granular"``;
74	    everything else → ``"elementwise_even"``.
75	
76	    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unknown optimizer (loud, no silent default —
77	    same discipline as the kernel dispatch, design §1.3).
78	    """
79	    if isinstance(opt, int):
80	        if opt not in _OPTID_TO_NAME:
81	            raise ValueError(f"unknown OptId {opt!r} (expected 0..10)")
82	        name = _OPTID_TO_NAME[opt]
83	    else:
84	        name = str(opt).strip().lower()
85	    if name in PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS:
86	        return _MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR
87	    if name in ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS:
88	        return _MODE_ELEMENTWISE
89	    raise ValueError(
90	        f"unknown optimizer {opt!r} — not in the 11-optimizer taxonomy "
91	        f"(elementwise={sorted(ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS)}, "
92	        f"per_tensor={sorted(PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS)})"
93	    )
94	
95	
96	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
97	#  Result types.
98	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
99	
100	
101	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
102	class TensorPlacement:
103	    """One tensor's whole-tensor placement under tensor-granular sharding.
104	
105	    ``name``/``numel`` identify the tensor; ``rank`` is the DP rank that owns it
106	    in full (no split). Tensor-granular sharding emits one of these per tensor.
107	    """
108	
109	    name: str
110	    numel: int
111	    rank: int
112	
113	
114	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
115	class ShardPlan:
116	    """A partition result: each rank's owned (name, start, end) flat slices.
117	
118	    ``slices[r]`` is the list of ``(name, start, end)`` slices rank ``r`` owns
119	    (``end`` exclusive, in the tensor's OWN flat index space). For tensor-granular
120	    mode every slice is a whole tensor ``(name, 0, numel)``; for elementwise mode
121	    a tensor may appear on several ranks as contiguous sub-slices.
122	
123	    ``mode`` is ``"elementwise_even"`` or ``"tensor_granular"``. ``rank_numel[r]``
124	    is the total element count rank ``r`` owns (the balance metric).
125	    """
126	
127	    mode: str
128	    world: int
129	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]]
130	    rank_numel: List[int]
131	
132	    @property
133	    def total_numel(self) -> int:
134	        return sum(self.rank_numel)
135	
136	    def imbalance(self) -> float:
137	        """max/mean rank load (1.0 == perfectly balanced; higher == lumpier).
138	
139	        Tensor-granular is necessarily lumpier than elementwise (whole tensors
140	        can't be split), so this is the "honest cost, measure it" number design
141	        §3.4 calls for. Returns 1.0 for the degenerate world<=1.
142	        """
143	        if self.world <= 1 or self.total_numel == 0:
144	            return 1.0
145	        mean = self.total_numel / self.world
146	        return max(self.rank_numel) / mean if mean > 0 else 1.0
147	
148	
149	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
150	#  Elementwise flat partition (design §2.4).
151	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
152	
153	
154	def even_partition(numel: int, world: int, rank: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
155	    """Contiguous, padded-even partition of ``numel`` across ``world`` ranks.
156	
157	    Byte-for-byte the convention of ``distributed._even_partition`` (the
158	    DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 flat-partition): each rank owns ``ceil(numel/world)``
159	    elements (last rank clamped), so the union covers ``[0, numel)`` exactly with
160	    no overlap. Mirrored here (not imported) so this pure-Python module needs no
161	    torch import; a unit test asserts it agrees with ``distributed`` when torch
162	    is present.
163	    """
164	    if world <= 1:
165	        return 0, numel
166	    per = (numel + world - 1) // world
167	    start = min(rank * per, numel)
168	    end = min(start + per, numel)
169	    return start, end
170	
171	
172	def partition_elementwise_even(
173	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int
174	) -> ShardPlan:
175	    """ELEMENTWISE shard: split each tensor's flat buffer evenly across ranks.
176	
177	    The finer partition (design §2.4) — best balance, valid for the elementwise
178	    optimizers (adamw/lion/grokfast/neuralgrok + the elementwise core of
179	    grokadamw/looksam/prodigy). A tensor MAY be split across ranks (that's fine:
180	    every per-element apply is local).
181	
182	    ``named_sizes`` is ``[(name, numel), ...]`` (e.g. from ``named_parameters()``
183	    sizes). Returns a :class:`ShardPlan` in ``"elementwise_even"`` mode.
184	    """
185	    world = max(1, int(world))
186	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(world)]
187	    rank_numel = [0] * world
188	    for name, numel in named_sizes:
189	        numel = int(numel)
190	        if numel < 0:
191	            raise ValueError(f"tensor {name!r} has negative numel {numel}")
192	        for r in range(world):
193	            s, e = even_partition(numel, world, r)
194	            if e > s:
195	                slices[r].append((name, s, e))
196	                rank_numel[r] += e - s
197	    return ShardPlan(_MODE_ELEMENTWISE, world, slices, rank_numel)
198	
199	
200	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	#  Tensor-granular partition (design §3.4) — the new requirement.
202	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	
204	
205	def partition_tensor_granular(
206	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int
207	) -> ShardPlan:
208	    """Assign WHOLE tensors to ranks (greedy by numel, balanced) — design §3.4.
209	
210	    No tensor is split across ranks, which is REQUIRED for the per-tensor
211	    optimizers (muon/SuperGrok11/SuperGrok15/SuperGrok2): their P2.x stages need
212	    the whole matrix/tensor on one rank (design §0.4/§2.4), and the co-located
213	    optimizer state (m/mu/sharpness/slow/gru_state) rides with its tensor.
214	
215	    ALGORITHM — greedy longest-processing-time (LPT): sort tensors descending by
216	    numel, then assign each to the currently least-loaded rank. This is the
217	    standard balanced whole-item bin-packing heuristic; it is deterministic
218	    (a pure function of the size list + world — design §2.7 requires deterministic
219	    shard boundaries) and gives a good (not optimal) balance. Ties broken by the
220	    lowest rank index, then by tensor name, so the result is stable across runs.
221	
222	    Balance is necessarily lumpier than elementwise (the embedding + ff matrices
223	    dominate), so :meth:`ShardPlan.imbalance` is the honest DP-efficiency cost
224	    design §3.4 says to measure.
225	
226	    ``named_sizes`` is ``[(name, numel), ...]``. Returns a :class:`ShardPlan` in
227	    ``"tensor_granular"`` mode where every owned slice is a whole tensor
228	    ``(name, 0, numel)``.
229	    """
230	    world = max(1, int(world))
231	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(world)]
232	    rank_numel = [0] * world
233	
234	    # Validate + materialize.
235	    tensors: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
236	    for name, numel in named_sizes:
237	        numel = int(numel)
238	        if numel < 0:
239	            raise ValueError(f"tensor {name!r} has negative numel {numel}")
240	        tensors.append((name, numel))
241	
242	    # LPT: descending by numel; tie-break by name so the order is total + stable.
243	    order = sorted(tensors, key=lambda t: (-t[1], t[0]))
244	    for name, numel in order:
245	        # Least-loaded rank; ties → lowest rank index (min() is stable on the
246	        # (load, rank) key).
247	        r = min(range(world), key=lambda k: (rank_numel[k], k))
248	        slices[r].append((name, 0, numel))
249	        rank_numel[r] += numel
250	
251	    # Keep each rank's slice list in the input (named_parameters()) order, so the
252	    # owned slices are reported in a stable, layout-meaningful order (the kernel
253	    # addresses tensors in named_parameters() order — decoder_layout.cuh).
254	    input_order = {name: i for i, (name, _) in enumerate(tensors)}
255	    for r in range(world):
256	        slices[r].sort(key=lambda sl: input_order[sl[0]])
257	
258	    return ShardPlan(_MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR, world, slices, rank_numel)
259	
260	
261	def partition_for_optimizer(
262	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int, opt
263	) -> ShardPlan:
264	    """Pick the partition mode from the optimizer (design §3.4) and run it.
265	
266	    Convenience wrapper: per-tensor cells → :func:`partition_tensor_granular`;
267	    elementwise cells → :func:`partition_elementwise_even`.
268	    """
269	    mode = shard_mode_for_optimizer(opt)
270	    if mode == _MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR:
271	        return partition_tensor_granular(named_sizes, world)
272	    return partition_elementwise_even(named_sizes, world)

1	"""tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py — Phase-2 sharded-optimizer bit-parity gate.
2	
3	IMPLEMENTS /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §7.3 (DELIVERABLE 1, task #25): at
4	DP=1 the new ZeRO-2/3 ``sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt>`` over the FULL param set
5	must produce **BIT-IDENTICAL** params to the in-kernel P3 fused tail
6	(``apply_optimizer<Opt>`` work-steal loop) on the SAME ``(params, grad, state)``.
7	This proves the B2-seam cut (design §2.2 — the ``if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad)
8	return;`` that ends the fused kernel at "local grad assembled" so a SEPARATE
9	sharded-opt kernel consumes the reduce-scattered grad) is correctness-preserving
10	PER OPTIMIZER, entirely on one GPU.
11	
12	THE EQUIVALENT CHECK (design §7.3 / the task's harvesting note). Harvesting the
13	pre-P3 (params, grad, state) through the public ABI is awkward (the fused step is
14	ONE launch that runs P0..P3), so we use the equivalence the task spells out:
15	
16	  1. Run ONE production fused step (in-kernel P3) on a freshly-built cell, with
17	     ``return_grad=True`` → ``params_after`` (scattered back into the model) AND
18	     the deterministically-reduced ``grad`` the P3 tail consumed (the dispatch.py
19	     fused path returns ``grad_out``). Snapshot ``params_before`` first.
20	  2. Re-run the SAME optimizer step routed through the sharded kernel: feed
21	     ``params_before`` + the captured ``grad`` + a ZERO-init ``[m|v|extra]`` state
22	     (the production state cache zero-inits at step 1) + the SAME scalars
23	     (``_opt_scalars_from`` — the single source the production path uses) into
24	     ``sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt>`` over the whole flat ``[0,total)``.
25	  3. Assert ``params_sharded`` is BITWISE-equal to ``params_after`` (and the
26	     updated m/v state matches the kernel's state slices bit-for-bit).
27	
28	WHY IT IS BIT-IDENTICAL, NOT MERELY ULP-EQUAL (so the assert is ``torch.equal``,
29	not a tol): the sharded kernel includes ``opt_components.cuh`` VERBATIM and calls
30	the EXACT SAME ``apply_optimizer<Opt>`` device function the P3 tail calls. The
31	only structural difference is the iteration shape — P3 work-steals the 30 tensors
32	and ``rebase_state``-offsets the per-element pointers per tensor; the sharded
33	kernel is a flat grid-stride over ``[0,total)`` with the un-rebased flat slices.
34	But ``rebase_state`` only ADDS the tensor offset to the per-element pointers
35	(``exp_avg``/``exp_avg_sq``/``ema``) and passes every scalar through unchanged
36	(fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:147), so element ``i`` always pairs ``params[i]`` ↔
37	``grad[i]`` ↔ ``m[i]`` ↔ ``v[i]`` ↔ ``ema[i]`` with the IDENTICAL scalars on both
38	paths. Same inputs + same device op (same ``--use_fast_math``/fp32 contraction) ⇒
39	same bits. The grokfast cold-start (``if (step==1) ema[idx]=grad[idx]``) is in
40	``apply_optimizer`` too, so it replicates exactly. MEASURED: maxd == 0.0 for every
41	cell below (no loosening was needed — see the run output).
42	
43	SCOPE — the ELEMENTWISE OptIds (design §2.3 / §0.4): ``{adamw, lion, grokfast}``.
44	These are the cells whose sharded-opt kernel is the flat grid-stride (their
45	``apply_optimizer<Opt>`` is purely per-element). The per-TENSOR cells
46	(muon/SG11/SG15/SG2) and the global-scalar cells (prodigy/grokadamw/looksam) need
47	an UPSTREAM stage / all-reduce before the flat apply (design §2.3/§2.4), out of
48	scope for this flat-kernel gate; their sharded path is the *full* persistent
49	kernel restricted to the owned tensors, validated separately. We run the three
50	elementwise ids across ALL THREE models (decoder/vit/mamba) so the cut is gated
51	on every L3-TC fwd+bwd substrate.
52	
53	JIT BUILD (task #25): the sharded kernel is bound via
54	``torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`` into its OWN build dir under
55	``/workspace/.torch_ext`` — it does NOT touch the production ``_ops`` build. The
56	binding TU (tests/hw/sharded_optimizer_binding.cu) owns its own
57	``PYBIND11_MODULE`` and is excluded from the setup.py glob by
58	``_owns_extension_module``.
59	
60	Run:
61	    PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py -q -s
62	    PYTHONPATH=. python tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py
63	"""
64	from __future__ import annotations
65	
66	import os
67	import sys
68	
69	import pytest
70	
71	try:
72	    import torch
73	    _HAS_TORCH = True
74	except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
75	    _HAS_TORCH = False
76	
77	_THIS = os.path.abspath(__file__)
78	_REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(_THIS), "..", ".."))
79	_BINDING_CU = os.path.join(_REPO, "tests", "hw", "sharded_optimizer_binding.cu")
80	# Own JIT build dir — NEVER the production _ops build (task #25 mandate).
81	_TORCH_EXT_DIR = os.environ.get("SG_TORCH_EXT_DIR", "/workspace/.torch_ext")
82	_BUILD_DIR = os.path.join(_TORCH_EXT_DIR, "sharded_opt_bind")
83	
84	
85	def _sm90a_available() -> bool:
86	    if not _HAS_TORCH or not torch.cuda.is_available():
87	        return False
88	    major, _ = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)
89	    return major >= 9
90	
91	
92	# hw + skipif gate — mirrors test_decoder_tc / test_l3tc_tail_gate discipline.
93	_GATE = pytest.mark.skipif(
94	    not _sm90a_available(),
95	    reason="sharded-optimizer bit-parity gate needs an sm_90 (Hopper) GPU + bf16")
96	
97	# OptId integers (mirror opt_components.cuh::OptId) for the elementwise ids.
98	_OPTID = {"adamw": 0, "lion": 1, "grokfast": 2}
99	
100	# (optimizer, model) cells — the 3 elementwise ids × the 3 L3-TC models. All run
101	# on the wgmma (bf16 tensor-core) production path (the only L3-TC engine).
102	_CELLS = [
103	    (opt, model)
104	    for model in ("decoder", "vit", "mamba")
105	    for opt in ("adamw", "lion", "grokfast")
106	]
107	
108	_MODULE = None
109	
110	
111	def _build_binding():
112	    """JIT-build the sharded-opt binding into /workspace/.torch_ext (NOT _ops)."""
113	    global _MODULE
114	    if _MODULE is not None:
115	        return _MODULE
116	    os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
117	    os.makedirs(_BUILD_DIR, exist_ok=True)
118	    from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load
119	    # The SAME flags the production build uses for the TC TUs (setup.py): the math
120	    # must compile identically (--use_fast_math, -DWITH_CUDA, --expt-relaxed-
121	    # constexpr) or apply_optimizer<Opt> could round differently and break bit-
122	    # parity. Repo-root include for the "csrc/..."-relative #includes.
123	    _MODULE = load(
124	        name="sharded_opt_bind",
125	        sources=[_BINDING_CU],
126	        extra_include_paths=[_REPO],
127	        build_directory=_BUILD_DIR,
128	        extra_cuda_cflags=[
129	            "-O3", "-std=c++17", "--use_fast_math", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
130	            "-DWITH_CUDA",
131	            "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
132	            "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a",
133	            "-lineinfo",
134	        ],
135	        extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"],
136	        verbose=True,
137	    )
138	    return _MODULE
139	
140	
141	def _g():
142	    if _REPO not in sys.path:
143	        sys.path.insert(0, _REPO)
144	    import grokking_race_v2 as g
145	    return g
146	
147	
148	def _build_cell(model, seed=42):
149	    """Build the live race model + one real batch (the SAME recipe the tail gate
150	    uses). Reseeds immediately before build_model so the init is byte-stable."""
151	    g = _g()
152	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
153	    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
154	              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,
155	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10, "p": 97})
156	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
157	    data = tuple(d.to(dev) for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, seed))
158	    torch.manual_seed(seed)
159	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
160	    m = g.build_model(c, dev)
161	    return g, c, m, data, dev
162	
163	
164	def _make_optimizer(opt, g, params, c):
165	    """The REAL production optimizer with the EXACT race hyperparameters (the
166	    source of the scalars _opt_scalars_from feeds the kernel)."""
167	    if opt == "adamw":
168	        return torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
169	                                 weight_decay=c["weight_decay"])
170	    if opt == "lion":
171	        return g.Lion(params, lr=c.get("lion_lr", 3e-4), betas=(c["beta1"], 0.99),
172	                      weight_decay=c.get("lion_wd", 3.0))
173	    if opt == "grokfast":
174	        return g.Grokfast(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
175	                          weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
176	                          grokfast_alpha=c.get("grokfast_alpha", 0.98),
177	                          grokfast_lamb=c.get("grokfast_lamb", 2.0))
178	    raise ValueError(f"unhandled elementwise opt {opt!r}")
179	
180	
181	def _flat_params(named, total, dev):
182	    out = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
183	    off = 0
184	    for _, p in named:
185	        n = p.numel()
186	        out[off:off + n].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1))
187	        off += n
188	    return out
189	
190	
191	def run_sharded_parity(opt, model, verbose=True):
192	    """Run the DP=1 sharded-opt-vs-P3 bit-parity check for one cell.
193	
194	    Returns (ok, detail). ok is True iff params AND m/v state are BITWISE-equal.
195	    """
196	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (fused_train_step, canonicalize_model,
197	                                              has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
198	                                              _opt_scalars_from)
199	    mod = _build_binding()
200	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
201	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
202	    # Precondition: the cell must really be wired L3-TC wgmma — else the gate is
203	    # comparing against the wrong tail.
204	    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{opt}/{model}: not L3-REAL (wire it first)"
205	    eng = gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16")
206	    assert eng == "wgmma", f"{opt}/{model}: bf16 engine is {eng!r}, expected wgmma"
207	
208	    named = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
209	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named)
210	    params_before = _flat_params(named, total, dev)
211	
212	    # ── (1) ONE production fused step (in-kernel P3), harvest grad + params_after.
213	    opt_obj = _make_optimizer(opt, g, m.parameters(), c)
214	    cache = {}
215	    loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, data[0], data[1],
216	                                  state_cache=cache, step=1, return_grad=True,
217	                                  gemm_impl="wgmma")
218	    params_after = _flat_params(named, total, dev)
219	    kstate = cache[canon]["state"]            # the kernel's [m|v|extra]+loss buffer
220	
221	    # ── (2) re-run the SAME step through the sharded kernel on the captured grad.
222	    #    ZERO-init [m|v|extra] state (matches the production cache cold-start);
223	    #    SAME scalars via _opt_scalars_from (the single source dispatch.py uses).
224	    sc = _opt_scalars_from(opt_obj, 1)
225	    params_sharded = params_before.clone()
226	    grad_in = grad.clone()                    # also lets us assert grad is NOT mutated
227	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
228	    mod.sharded_opt_step(
229	        _OPTID[opt], params_sharded, grad_in, state,
230	        sc["lr"], sc["beta1"], sc["beta2"], sc["eps"], sc["weight_decay"],
231	        sc["bc1"], sc["bc2"], sc.get("alpha", 0.98), sc.get("lamb", 2.0), 1)
232	
233	    # ── (3) BITWISE-equality asserts (no tol — the math is the same device op).
234	    param_eq = torch.equal(params_sharded, params_after)
235	    param_maxd = (params_sharded - params_after).abs().max().item()
236	    m_eq = torch.equal(state[0:total], kstate[0:total])
237	    v_eq = torch.equal(state[total:2 * total], kstate[total:2 * total])
238	    grad_unmutated = torch.equal(grad_in, grad)   # the sharded apply must NOT write grad
239	    ok = param_eq and m_eq and v_eq and grad_unmutated
240	    if verbose:
241	        print(f"  [{opt}/{model}] params bit-eq={param_eq} maxd={param_maxd:.3e} | "
242	              f"m_eq={m_eq} v_eq={v_eq} | grad_unmutated={grad_unmutated} | "
243	              f"loss={loss:.5f} total={total}", flush=True)
244	    return ok, dict(param_eq=param_eq, param_maxd=param_maxd, m_eq=m_eq, v_eq=v_eq,

1	"""tests/hw/test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py — DP=2 NCCL-loopback cross-rank A/A/A.
2	
3	IMPLEMENTS /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §7.1 (single-rank/multi-rank NCCL
4	loopback correctness of the B2-seam decomposition) + §6.4 (THE cross-rank
5	bit-determinism gate) at **DP=2 on ONE GPU** (task #25 DELIVERABLE 2). Both ranks
6	run on cuda:0 (``CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`` for both), giving a REAL 2-rank
7	reduce/all-gather sharing one GPU — the collective wiring + the cross-rank
8	determinism gate validated WITHOUT a second GPU, before the 8×H100 window.
9	
10	THE DECOMPOSED STEP per rank (design §2.1 [1]..[4], cut at the B2 seam §0.1):
11	    [1] production fused step on THIS rank's batch shard -> local grad[total]
12	        (the dispatch.py fused path returns grad_out; the in-kernel P3 runs too,
13	         but we IGNORE its param update and re-apply via the sharded kernel on the
14	         REDUCED grad — the ZeRO>=2 "kernel ends at local grad" cut, design §2.2)
15	    [2] reduce the per-rank grads across DP  -> each rank's OWNED grad shard
16	    [3] sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> (DELIVERABLE 1) over the OWNED shard
17	    [4] all-gather params  -> full updated params on every rank
18	
19	NCCL MULTI-RANK-ONE-GPU (the loopback enabler). NCCL 2.20.5 REFUSES two ranks on
20	one physical device by default ("Duplicate GPU detected : rank 0 and rank 1 both
21	on CUDA device …", ncclInvalidUsage) — its communicator init dedups by (hostid,
22	PCI-busid). The documented loopback workaround is to give each rank a DISTINCT
23	``NCCL_HOSTID`` so the pair differs and NCCL treats the ranks as different
24	"nodes"; the collectives then run for-real on the shared device (correctness, not
25	perf — exactly the design §7.1 [SPEC] note). We set it per rank in
26	``_init_dist`` BEFORE init_process_group. (Measured: with the hostid trick,
27	all_gather_into_tensor + reduce_scatter_tensor both succeed on one H100.)
28	
29	FIXED-ORDER REDUCE (the A/A/A non-negotiable, design §2.7/§6.4). NCCL's
30	ring/tree ``reduce_scatter`` float-summation order is NOT guaranteed bit-identical
31	run-to-run, which would break the cross-rank A/A/A gate. So for the grad reduce we
32	use the design's mandated **fixed-order/reduce-to-rank pattern**: NCCL
33	``all_gather`` the full per-rank grad (a PURE data movement → bit-exact, order-
34	free), then sum the gathered grads in **ascending rank order** locally in fp32 —
35	the cross-rank analogue of the in-kernel ascending-CTA fp32 sum that made the
36	single-GPU path A/A/A (dispatch.py:805-833). This is what makes (b) below pass.
37	We use ``ZeRO3Sharder``/``even_partition`` for the shard-ownership convention
38	(design §0.5 reuse) but do the reduce fixed-order (the §2.7 correction the raw
39	NCCL reduce-scatter needs).
40	
41	THE THREE ASSERTS (design §6.4):
42	  (a) the final all-gathered params are IDENTICAL on both ranks (the shard dance
43	      reconstitutes the same full param on every rank);
44	  (b) repeating the WHOLE run 3× is BIT-IDENTICAL (the cross-rank A/A/A gate —
45	      fixed-order reduce + deterministic shard boundaries make it structural);
46	  (c) DP=2-loopback vs the single-GPU fused step on the UNSHARDED batch: NOT
47	      required bitwise (the grad reduce order differs — the unsharded kernel sums
48	      all B rows in one ascending-CTA pass; the DP=2 path sums two half-batch
49	      grads). Asserted within the parity tol (SG-family ~3e-5 fp32, campaign
50	      baseline) and the ACTUAL delta is reported.
51	
52	GRAPH CAPTURE (design §7.4) lives in test_step_graph_capture.py (a sibling file).

103	def _init_dist():
104	    """Init a 2-rank NCCL group with BOTH ranks on cuda:0 (the loopback trick)."""
105	    import torch.distributed as dist
106	    rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
107	    # DISTINCT NCCL_HOSTID per rank defeats NCCL 2.20.5's duplicate-GPU dedup so
108	    # two ranks can share cuda:0 (design §7.1 multi-rank-one-GPU). Must precede
109	    # init_process_group. P2P/SHM off is harmless here (one device, no real peer).
110	    os.environ["NCCL_HOSTID"] = f"sg-loopback-rank-{rank}"
111	    os.environ.setdefault("NCCL_P2P_DISABLE", "1")
112	    os.environ.setdefault("NCCL_SHM_DISABLE", "1")
113	    # Block collectives on the HOST (not a GPU busy-spin) so a momentarily-slower
114	    # rank does not starve the other's full-GPU persistent megakernel on the shared
115	    # device — the second guard (with the symmetric-work structure) against the
116	    # collective-vs-megakernel contention of the loopback config.
117	    os.environ.setdefault("NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT", "1")
118	    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT", "1")
119	    torch.cuda.set_device(0)

164	def _shard_batch(tokens, targets, world, rank):
165	    """Deterministically split a fixed batch's ROWS across ranks via the
166	    shard_map even-partition helper (design §7.1 "shard a fixed batch
167	    deterministically"). Each shard is truncated to a multiple of 16 so the wgmma
168	    dW K-loop accepts it (dispatch.py truncates B%16 internally too, but we make
169	    each shard ÷16 up front so the two shards are balanced + comparable)."""
170	    from grokking_optimizers.parallel.shard_map import even_partition
171	    B = int(tokens.shape[0])
172	    # Round the whole batch down to a multiple of 16*world so each rank's slice is
173	    # a multiple of 16 (clean wgmma tiles, no per-rank truncation drift).
174	    step = 16 * world
175	    Bw = B - (B % step)
176	    s, e = even_partition(Bw, world, rank)
177	    return tokens[s:e].contiguous(), targets[s:e].contiguous(), Bw

180	def _fixed_order_allreduce_grad(dist, grad, world):
181	    """FIXED-ORDER cross-rank grad reduce (design §2.7/§6.4): NCCL all_gather the
182	    full per-rank grad (pure movement, bit-exact), then sum in ASCENDING rank
183	    order in fp32. Returns the full reduced grad (same on every rank). Averaged by
184	    world (DDP/ZeRO convention — matches ZeRO3Sharder.reduce_scatter_grads's div)."""
185	    total = grad.numel()
186	    gathered = torch.empty(total * world, dtype=grad.dtype, device=grad.device)
187	    # Sync the local megakernel to completion BEFORE the collective so the two
188	    # never overlap on the shared device (the loopback lockstep).
189	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
190	    dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, grad.contiguous())
191	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
192	    acc = torch.zeros(total, dtype=torch.float32, device=grad.device)
193	    for r in range(world):                       # ascending rank order — fixed
194	        acc += gathered[r * total:(r + 1) * total]
195	    acc /= float(world)
196	    return acc
197

199	def _run_decomposed_step(dist, rank, world, g, c, m, data, dev, opt, mod,
200	                         init_flat=None):
201	    """ONE DP=2 decomposed step. Returns (full_params_after, loss_local, Bw).
202	
203	    If ``init_flat`` is given, the model's params are RESET to it before the step
204	    (so an A/A/A re-run starts from byte-identical init WITHOUT rebuilding the
205	    model — faster, and an equally-rigorous A/A/A: the whole decomposed step
206	    re-runs from the same init). When None, the model's current params are the
207	    init (the first run)."""
208	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (fused_train_step, canonicalize_model,
209	                                              _opt_scalars_from)
210	    from grokking_optimizers.parallel.shard_map import even_partition
211	    canon = canonicalize_model(model_of(c))
212	    named = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
213	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named)
214	
215	    # Reset params to the shared init (if provided) so every A/A/A run + every rank
216	    # starts from the SAME weights. Then snapshot params_before.
217	    if init_flat is not None:
218	        off = 0
219	        for _, p in named:
220	            n = p.numel(); p.data.reshape(-1).copy_(init_flat[off:off + n]); off += n
221	    pb = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
222	    off = 0
223	    for _, p in named:
224	        n = p.numel(); pb[off:off + n].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); off += n
225	
226	    # [1] production fused step on THIS rank's batch shard -> local grad[total].
227	    #     (in-kernel P3 also runs and mutates p.data; we restore pb below and
228	    #      re-apply via the sharded kernel on the REDUCED grad — the §2.2 cut.)
229	    tok_sh, tgt_sh, Bw = _shard_batch(data[0], data[1], world, rank)
230	    opt_obj = _make_optimizer(opt, g, m.parameters(), c)
231	    cache = {}
232	    loss, grad_local = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tok_sh, tgt_sh,
233	                                        state_cache=cache, step=1, return_grad=True,
234	                                        gemm_impl="wgmma")
235	
236	    # [2] FIXED-ORDER reduce of the per-rank grads across DP -> full reduced grad.
237	    grad_full = _fixed_order_allreduce_grad(dist, grad_local, world)
238	
239	    # [3] sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> over THIS rank's OWNED param/grad/state
240	    #     shard. ZeRO-3 element-even partition (design §2.4 — elementwise opt).
241	    s, e = even_partition(total, world, rank)
242	    shard_numel = e - s
243	    sc = _opt_scalars_from(opt_obj, 1)
244	    full = pb.clone()                             # start from params_before
245	    params_shard = full[s:e].contiguous()
246	    grad_shard = grad_full[s:e].contiguous()
247	    # Owned shard of the zero-init [m|v|extra] state (laid out [m|v|ema] over the
248	    # shard so the binding's m=state[0:n]/v=state[n:2n]/ema=state[2n:3n] aligns).
249	    state_shard = torch.zeros(3 * shard_numel, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
250	    mod.sharded_opt_step(
251	        _OPTID[opt], params_shard, grad_shard, state_shard,
252	        sc["lr"], sc["beta1"], sc["beta2"], sc["eps"], sc["weight_decay"],
253	        sc["bc1"], sc["bc2"], sc.get("alpha", 0.98), sc.get("lamb", 2.0), 1)
254	
255	    # [4] all-gather the updated param shards -> full params on every rank. Use a
256	    #     PADDED all_gather_into_tensor over the even partition (uniform per-rank
257	    #     length), then stitch (mirrors ZeRO3Sharder.all_gather_params' convention).
258	    per = (total + world - 1) // world
259	    buf = torch.zeros(per, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
260	    buf[:shard_numel].copy_(params_shard)
261	    gathered = torch.empty(per * world, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
262	    torch.cuda.synchronize()                      # sharded-opt done before collective
263	    dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, buf)
264	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
265	    out = torch.empty(total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
266	    for r in range(world):
267	        rs = min(r * per, total); re = min(rs + per, total)
268	        n = re - rs
269	        if n > 0:
270	            out[rs:re].copy_(gathered[r * per:r * per + n])
271	    return out, float(loss), Bw
272

274	# Helper: the canonical model name is carried on c (set in _build_cell).
275	def model_of(c):
276	    return c["model_type"]

279	def _single_gpu_reference(g, c, m, data, dev, opt, world, init_flat):
280	    """The single-GPU fused step on the UNSHARDED (full) batch — assert (c). Resets
281	    ``m`` to the SAME init the workers used, then runs the in-kernel-P3 fused step
282	    on the SAME truncated batch the two shards together cover (Bw rows). The result
283	    is the in-kernel P3 update over the FULL-batch grad (vs the DP=2 path's
284	    averaged two-half-batch grad — they agree up to float reduction order)."""
285	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import fused_train_step, canonicalize_model
286	    canon = canonicalize_model(model_of(c))
287	    named = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
288	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named)
289	    # Reset to the shared init.
290	    off = 0
291	    for _, p in named:
292	        n = p.numel(); p.data.reshape(-1).copy_(init_flat[off:off + n]); off += n
293	    # Same Bw the workers cover (B rounded to 16*world).
294	    B = int(data[0].shape[0]); step = 16 * world; Bw = B - (B % step)
295	    opt_obj = _make_optimizer(opt, g, m.parameters(), c)
296	    cache = {}
297	    fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, data[0][:Bw], data[1][:Bw],
298	                     state_cache=cache, step=1, return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
299	    out = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
300	    off = 0
301	    for _, p in named:
302	        n = p.numel(); out[off:off + n].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); off += n
303	    return out
304	
305	
306	def worker_main(opt, model):
307	    """The torchrun worker: run the DP=2 decomposed step 3× (A/A/A), assert (a)+(b)
308	    on every rank and (c) on rank 0. Prints a per-rank summary; exits non-zero on
309	    any failure (the pytest harness asserts the exit code)."""
310	    dist, rank, world = _init_dist()
311	    assert world == 2, f"expected world=2, got {world}"
312	    mod = _build_sharded_binding()
313	
314	    # Build the cell ONCE (same seed on every rank ⇒ byte-identical init + the SAME
315	    # fixed batch), and snapshot the initial flat params. Each A/A/A run RESETS the
316	    # model to this snapshot before the decomposed step (faster than rebuilding,
317	    # and an equally-rigorous A/A/A — the whole step re-runs from the same init).
318	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
319	    named0 = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
320	    init_flat = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named0]).clone()
321	
322	    # Run the whole decomposed pipeline 3× from the SAME init (the A/A/A gate: the
323	    # only thing under test is run-to-run non-determinism).
324	    runs = []
325	    losses = []
326	    for _ in range(3):
327	        full, loss, Bw = _run_decomposed_step(dist, rank, world, g, c, m, data,
328	                                               dev, opt, mod, init_flat=init_flat)
329	        runs.append(full)
330	        losses.append(loss)
331	
332	    # (b) A/A/A: the 3 full-param results are BIT-IDENTICAL on THIS rank.
333	    aaa_ok = bool(torch.equal(runs[0], runs[1]) and torch.equal(runs[1], runs[2]))
334	
335	    # (a) cross-rank identity: the final params match the OTHER rank's, bit-for-bit.
336	    # all_gather the run-0 full params from both ranks and compare.
337	    total = runs[0].numel()
338	    gathered = torch.empty(total * world, dtype=torch.float32, device=runs[0].device)
339	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
340	    dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, runs[0].contiguous())
341	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
342	    rank0_params = gathered[0:total]
343	    rank1_params = gathered[total:2 * total]
344	    cross_ok = bool(torch.equal(rank0_params, rank1_params))
345	
346	    # (c) vs single-GPU unsharded reference. BOTH ranks compute it (only rank 0 uses
347	    # it for the assert) so the megakernel work stays SYMMETRIC across ranks — this
348	    # is the multi-rank-one-GPU lockstep that avoids the NCCL-collective-vs-persistent-
349	    # megakernel starvation: one rank busy-spinning in a collective while the other is
350	    # still in a full-GPU megakernel deadlocks the shared device. Keeping every rank's
351	    # device timeline identical (same fused steps, same collectives, in the same order)
352	    # is what makes the loopback progress (the simple fused→all_gather probe proved
353	    # lockstep works; the asymmetric rank0-only reference is what hung).
354	    ref = _single_gpu_reference(g, c, m, data, dev, opt, world, init_flat)
355	    delta_c = (runs[0] - ref).abs().max().item()
356	    denom = ref.abs().max().item() + 1e-30
357	    rel_c = delta_c / denom
358	    parity_c = bool(rel_c < _PARITY_TOL)
359	    if rank == 0:
360	        print(f"[dp2-loopback rank0] {opt}/{model}: (a) cross-rank bit-eq={cross_ok} | "
361	              f"(b) A/A/A bit-eq={aaa_ok} | (c) vs single-GPU unsharded: "
362	              f"maxd={delta_c:.3e} rel={rel_c:.3e} (tol {_PARITY_TOL:.0e}) "
363	              f"parity={parity_c} | loss_shard={losses[0]:.5f}",
364	              flush=True)
365	    else:
366	        print(f"[dp2-loopback rank1] {opt}/{model}: (a) cross-rank bit-eq={cross_ok} | "
367	              f"(b) A/A/A bit-eq={aaa_ok} | loss_shard={losses[0]:.5f}", flush=True)
368	
369	    # Reduce a pass/fail bit across ranks (the design §6.3 "all ranks agree" check):
370	    # (a)+(b) must hold on EVERY rank; (c) is gated on rank 0's comparison (runs[0]
371	    # is rank 0's full params vs rank 0's reference) and broadcast so every rank
372	    # exits consistently.
373	    local_ok = 1 if (aaa_ok and cross_ok) else 0
374	    ok_t = torch.tensor([local_ok], dtype=torch.int32, device=runs[0].device)
375	    torch.cuda.synchronize()                       # reference megakernel done first
376	    dist.all_reduce(ok_t)                          # sum; must == world
377	    all_ranks_ok = int(ok_t.item()) == world
378	    c_t = torch.tensor([1 if parity_c else 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=runs[0].device)
379	    dist.broadcast(c_t, src=0)                      # rank-0's (c) verdict wins
380	    c_ok_all = int(c_t.item()) == 1
381	
382	    dist.barrier()
383	    dist.destroy_process_group()
384	
385	    if not (all_ranks_ok and c_ok_all):
386	        if rank == 0:
387	            print(f"[dp2-loopback] FAIL: all_ranks_ok={all_ranks_ok} "
388	                  f"(a+b) c_ok={c_ok_all} (c)", flush=True)
389	        return 1
390	    if rank == 0:
391	        print(f"[dp2-loopback] OK: {opt}/{model} — cross-rank identity + A/A/A "
392	              f"bit-exact on both ranks; (c) within parity tol.", flush=True)
393	    return 0
394

402	    import shutil

414	def _spawn_worker(opt, model, port):
415	    """Spawn torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 on cuda:0 for one cell; return CompletedProcess."""
416	    env = dict(os.environ)
417	    env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "0"           # BOTH ranks on cuda:0 (loopback)
418	    env["PYTHONPATH"] = _REPO + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")

436	@pytest.mark.parametrize("opt,model", _DP2_CELLS)
437	def test_dp2_loopback_cross_rank_aaa(opt, model):
438	    """torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 (both on cuda:0): the DP=2 decomposed step is
439	    cross-rank identical + A/A/A bit-exact, and within parity tol of the single-
440	    GPU unsharded step. Design §7.1 + §6.4."""
441	    port = 29610 + _DP2_CELLS.index((opt, model))
442	    proc = _spawn_worker(opt, model, port)
443	    # Surface the worker's stdout (the per-rank summary lines) for -s visibility.
444	    tail = "\n".join(proc.stdout.splitlines()[-25:])
445	    print(f"\n--- torchrun {opt}/{model} (rc={proc.returncode}) ---\n{tail}")
446	    if proc.returncode != 0:
447	        err_tail = "\n".join(proc.stderr.splitlines()[-40:])
448	        raise AssertionError(
449	            f"DP=2 loopback worker failed for {opt}/{model} (rc={proc.returncode}).\n"
450	            f"--- stdout tail ---\n{tail}\n--- stderr tail ---\n{err_tail}")

462	    ap.add_argument("--opt", default="adamw", choices=list(_OPTID))

3	// sharded-optimizer kernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh).
4	//
5	// PURPOSE (/workspace/.parallelism_design.md §7.3, task #25 DELIVERABLE 1): give
6	// tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py + test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py a real
7	// device entry point to `sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt>` for the ELEMENTWISE
8	// OptIds {adamw, lion, grokfast} so the DP=1 bit-parity check (sharded kernel ==
9	// in-kernel P3 fused tail on the SAME (params, grad, state)) can run on one GPU.
10	//
11	// IT IS NOT THE PRODUCTION BUILD. It is JIT-loaded via torch.utils.cpp_extension
12	// .load into its OWN build dir under /workspace/.torch_ext — it does NOT touch
13	// the production `_ops` extension (which the setup.py glob excludes anyway: this
14	// TU owns its own PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME …), and
15	// setup.py::_owns_extension_module drops exactly such standalone-JIT drivers).
16	//
17	// ZERO NEW MATH: it includes the header verbatim and reuses
18	// sg::fused::sm90::sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> + the canonical FusedOptState /
19	// apply_scalars from opt_components.cuh. The FusedOptState construction here is a
20	// 1:1 mirror of mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu's binding (state slices
21	// [m|v|extra] = [state | state+total | state+2*total]; apply_scalars then
22	// st.lr=lr), so the per-element apply at index i is byte-identical to the P3
23	// tail's apply at the same flat element — which is the whole point of §7.3.
24	// ============================================================================
25	
26	#include <torch/extension.h>
27	#include <c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h>
28	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
29	#include <cstdint>
30	
31	// Pulls in sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt,Par> + (transitively) OptId /
32	// FusedOptState / FusedScalars / apply_scalars / apply_optimizer<Opt>.
33	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh"
34	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/parallel_config.cuh"
35	
36	namespace {
37	
38	using sg::fused::sm90::FusedOptState;
39	using sg::fused::sm90::FusedScalars;
40	using sg::fused::sm90::OptId;
41	using sg::fused::sm90::apply_scalars;
42	using sg::fused::sm90::launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel;
43	using SingleGPU = sg::fused::par::SingleGPU;
44	
45	// Build the FusedScalars POD the same way dispatch.cpp does for the decoder TC
46	// path (csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp:893). Only the fields the elementwise tails
47	// read are non-default; everything else keeps the inert ABI default (the struct
48	// declares in-class defaults). bc1/bc2 are the UN-INVERTED bias corrections the
49	// host computes (1 - beta^step) — passed in so they match _opt_scalars_from
50	// byte-for-byte (the single source the production path uses).
51	FusedScalars make_scalars(double lr, double beta1, double beta2, double eps,
52	                          double wd, double bc1, double bc2,
53	                          double alpha, double lamb) {
54	    FusedScalars s;          // in-class defaults for every field
55	    s.lr    = static_cast<float>(lr);
56	    s.beta1 = static_cast<float>(beta1);
57	    s.beta2 = static_cast<float>(beta2);
58	    s.eps   = static_cast<float>(eps);
59	    s.wd    = static_cast<float>(wd);
60	    s.bc1   = static_cast<float>(bc1);
61	    s.bc2   = static_cast<float>(bc2);
62	    s.alpha = static_cast<float>(alpha);   // grokfast EMA decay (inert for adamw/lion)
63	    s.lamb  = static_cast<float>(lamb);    // grokfast amplification (inert for adamw/lion)
64	    return s;
65	}
66	
67	// Mirror of the TC launcher's FusedOptState binding (lines 138-185): the m/v/ema
68	// slices over the SAME flat [m|v|extra] state buffer, then apply_scalars + st.lr.
69	// `total` is the FULL param count (DP=1: the owned shard IS the whole param set).
70	FusedOptState make_state(float* state, int64_t total,
71	                         const FusedScalars& scalars, double lr) {
72	    FusedOptState st;
73	    st.exp_avg    = state;                 // m   = state[0      : total)
74	    st.exp_avg_sq = state + total;         // v   = state[total  : 2*total)
75	    st.ema        = state + 2 * total;     // ema = state[2*total: 3*total)  (grokfast)
76	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);            // un-frozen bc1/bc2 + alpha/lamb (+ inert rest)
77	    st.lr = static_cast<float>(lr);        // single source for the rate (matches P3)
78	    return st;
79	}
80	
81	// Dispatch the flat sharded kernel for an elementwise OptId. The kernel is a flat
82	// grid-stride over [0, shard_numel) calling apply_optimizer<Opt> — the EXACT P3
83	// math, no GridBarrier (design §2.3). DP=1: shard_numel == total.
84	void launch_for_opt(int opt_id, float* params, const float* grad, int64_t total,
85	                    const FusedOptState& st, double lr, int step,
86	                    cudaStream_t stream) {
87	    cudaError_t err = cudaSuccess;
88	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
89	        case OptId::AdamW:
90	            err = launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel<OptId::AdamW, SingleGPU>(
91	                params, grad, total, static_cast<float>(lr), step, st, stream);
92	            break;
93	        case OptId::Lion:
94	            err = launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel<OptId::Lion, SingleGPU>(
95	                params, grad, total, static_cast<float>(lr), step, st, stream);
96	            break;
97	        case OptId::Grokfast:
98	            err = launch_sharded_optimizer_kernel<OptId::Grokfast, SingleGPU>(
99	                params, grad, total, static_cast<float>(lr), step, st, stream);
100	            break;
101	        default:
102	            TORCH_CHECK(false,
103	                "sharded_optimizer_binding: opt_id ", opt_id, " is not one of the "
104	                "elementwise ids {adamw=0, lion=1, grokfast=2} this JIT binding "
105	                "instantiates (design §7.3 — the per-tensor cells need the full "
106	                "persistent kernel, not this flat shard).");
107	    }
108	    TORCH_CHECK(err == cudaSuccess,
109	        "sharded_optimizer_kernel launch failed: ", cudaGetErrorString(err));
110	}
111	
112	}  // namespace
113	
114	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
115	//  sharded_opt_step — run ONE sharded-optimizer step IN PLACE on `params`.
116	//
117	//  params : [total] fp32 owned param slice (DP=1: the whole flat param set),
118	//           MUTATED in place (the test compares it to the P3 fused tail's output).
119	//  grad   : [total] fp32 reduce-scattered grad (DP=1: the captured fused grad).
120	//  state  : [>= 3*total] fp32 [m|v|extra] state buffer (zero-init at step 1, as
121	//           the production state cache is). MUTATED in place (m/v/ema updated).
122	//  The scalars are passed positionally so the Python side computes them via the
123	//  SAME _opt_scalars_from the production path uses — guaranteeing bit-identity.
124	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
125	void sharded_opt_step(int64_t opt_id,
126	                      at::Tensor params, at::Tensor grad, at::Tensor state,
127	                      double lr, double beta1, double beta2, double eps,
128	                      double weight_decay, double bc1, double bc2,
129	                      double alpha, double lamb, int64_t step) {
130	    TORCH_CHECK(params.is_cuda() && grad.is_cuda() && state.is_cuda(),
131	                "sharded_opt_step: params/grad/state must be CUDA tensors");
132	    TORCH_CHECK(params.scalar_type() == at::kFloat &&
133	                grad.scalar_type() == at::kFloat &&
134	                state.scalar_type() == at::kFloat,
135	                "sharded_opt_step: params/grad/state must be float32");
136	    TORCH_CHECK(params.is_contiguous() && grad.is_contiguous() &&
137	                state.is_contiguous(),
138	                "sharded_opt_step: params/grad/state must be contiguous");
139	    const int64_t total = params.numel();
140	    TORCH_CHECK(grad.numel() == total,
141	                "sharded_opt_step: grad numel ", grad.numel(),
142	                " != params numel ", total);
143	    TORCH_CHECK(state.numel() >= 3 * total,
144	                "sharded_opt_step: state needs >= 3*total (", 3 * total,
145	                ") floats, got ", state.numel());
146	
147	    FusedScalars scalars = make_scalars(lr, beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay,
148	                                        bc1, bc2, alpha, lamb);
149	    FusedOptState st = make_state(state.data_ptr<float>(), total, scalars, lr);
150	
151	    cudaStream_t stream = c10::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream().stream();
152	    launch_for_opt(static_cast<int>(opt_id), params.data_ptr<float>(),
153	                   grad.data_ptr<float>(), total, st, lr,
154	                   static_cast<int>(step), stream);
155	}
156	
157	PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME, m) {
158	    m.doc() = "JIT binding for the ZeRO-2/3 sharded-optimizer kernel "
159	              "(design §7.3 bit-parity gate; elementwise OptIds only).";
160	    m.def("sharded_opt_step", &sharded_opt_step,
161	          "Run one sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt> step in place over the owned "
162	          "flat shard (opt_id in {0=adamw,1=lion,2=grokfast}).",
163	          py::arg("opt_id"), py::arg("params"), py::arg("grad"), py::arg("state"),
164	          py::arg("lr"), py::arg("beta1"), py::arg("beta2"), py::arg("eps"),
165	          py::arg("weight_decay"), py::arg("bc1"), py::arg("bc2"),
166	          py::arg("alpha"), py::arg("lamb"), py::arg("step"));
167	}

700	    """Bookkeeping for one parameter's flat slice owned by this DP rank.

703	    parameter's flattened buffer (and, symmetrically, the same slice of every
704	    optimizer-state tensor for that param). ``numel`` is the full param size.

718	    """Contiguous, padded-even partition of ``numel`` across ``world`` ranks.
719	
720	    Matches the DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 flat-partition convention: each rank owns
721	    ``ceil(numel/world)`` elements (the last rank's slice is clamped), so the
722	    union covers ``[0, numel)`` exactly with no overlap.
723	    """
724	    if world <= 1:

733	    """§8.3 ZeRO-3 full optimizer-state sharding across the DP group.
734	
735	    Two backends, auto-selected:
736	
737	    * **DeepSpeed** — when importable, ZeRO-3 is best handled by DeepSpeed's
738	      `deepspeed.initialize(...)` engine (partitioned params + reduce-scatter

740	      hand back the framework-managed shape and the megakernel adapter (§8.4)
741	      plugs in as the `client_optimizer`. :meth:`build_ds_config` emits the
742	      matching ZeRO-3 config dict.

744	    * **Native shim** — when DeepSpeed is absent, this class provides the same
745	      *pattern* with raw ``torch.distributed`` collectives:
746	
747	        - :meth:`partition_optimizer_state` assigns each DP rank a contiguous
748	          ``1/N`` slice of every param's optimizer state (m/v/etc.), so the
749	          aggregate state memory is ``1/N`` per rank — the win SG2's ~5–6×
750	          state footprint needs.

752	          ends up with the *reduced* gradient for **only its owned slice**
753	          (reduce-scatter), which is what the local optimizer step consumes.
754	        - :meth:`all_gather_params` reconstitutes the full parameter from the
755	          per-rank slices after the step (all-gather-on-step), so forward/
756	          backward see complete weights.

759	    (every collective short-circuits when DP size is 1 / no job launched).

762	    now uses the fused per-parameter ``reduce_scatter_tensor`` /
763	    ``all_gather_into_tensor`` primitives (half the traffic of the old
764	    all-reduce-then-slice, and one collective call instead of a Python list
765	    gather). It still issues **one collective per parameter**. A further win
766	    would coalesce many small params into a single flat ~``reduce_bucket_size``
767	    bucket per reduce-scatter/all-gather (as DeepSpeed's ``contiguous_gradients``
768	    does). That is NOT implemented here: a correct cross-param bucketed
769	    reduce-scatter must reproduce DeepSpeed's exact per-rank ownership of the
770	    *concatenated* buffer (padding + alignment so each rank's owned slice maps
771	    back to the right param sub-ranges), which is easy to get subtly wrong and
772	    cannot be validated without a real multi-GPU job. The risk outweighs the
773	    value for the race's small models, so it is deferred to the DeepSpeed path
774	    (``build_ds_config`` already sets ``contiguous_gradients=True`` and the
775	    bucket sizes). The DDP (ZeRO-0/1/2) path *is* bucketed — see

803

870	        owned slice** of each parameter — the input the sharded local optimizer
871	        step consumes. Falls back to a plain copy of the local grad slice when
872	        DP size is 1 / no job is launched (single-process correctness).
873	
874	        Implementation: a true fused ``reduce_scatter_tensor`` per parameter —
875	        each rank sends the whole (per-rank-padded) flat grad and receives only
876	        the reduced sum for its owned slice, which is half the traffic of the
877	        former ``all_reduce``-then-slice. The padded reduce-scatter convention
878	        matches :meth:`all_gather_params` / :meth:`_even_partition` (each rank
879	        owns ``ceil(numel/world)`` elements). Falls back to the local slice when
880	        DP size is 1 / no job is launched (single-process correctness).
881	        """

883	        live = self.dp_world > 1 and is_dist_available_and_initialized()
884	        ws = self.dp_world
885	        if not live:

893	        for name, g in named_grads:

8	// warp-specialization primitives (csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh).

13	// scripts/compile_to_object.sh) and degrading to a correct fallback on older
14	// arches so the codegen matrix still builds:
15	//
16	//   §1.1  TaskQueue        — a single global atomic work counter that every
17	//                            persistent CTA pulls parameter-tensor indices
18	//                            from (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern).
19	//   §1.2  work-stealing     — there is NO static partition: an idle CTA simply
20	//                            keeps calling TaskQueue::next(), so a CTA that
21	//                            finishes its tensor early steals the next one.
22	//                            (atomicAdd on the shared counter IS the steal.)
23	//   §1.3  sm_id()           — reads %smid so the host can pin one persistent
24	//                            CTA per SM and keep that SM's optimizer-state
25	//                            slice L2-warm across the step.

27	//                            global atomics + a sense-reversing generation
28	//                            counter. Reusable, needs NO cooperative launch
29	//                            (so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap).
30	//
31	// §1.14 fences: acquire/release are placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY — exactly
32	// one __threadfence() before the arrival publish and one acquire load after
33	// the release wait at the barrier, and one fence at the task hand-off. No loose
34	// fences (a loose fence here is both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun).
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

57	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
58	//
59	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
60	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
61	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
62	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
63	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
64	// =========================================================================
65	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
66	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
67	    unsigned id;
68	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
69	    return id;
70	#else
71	    return 0u;
72	#endif
73	}

75	// =========================================================================
76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};

119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
181	                __threadfence();
182	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
183	            } else {
184	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
185	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
187	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
189	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
190	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
191	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
192	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
193	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
194	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
195	                       == my_gen) {
196	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
197	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
198	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
199	#endif
200	                }
201	            }
202	
203	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
205	            __threadfence();
206	        }
207	
208	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
209	        __syncthreads();
210	    }
211	
212	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
214	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
215	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
216	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
217	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
218	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
219	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
220	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
221	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
222	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
223	        __syncthreads();
224	
225	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
226	            unsigned my_gen =
227	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
228	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
229	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
230	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
231	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
232	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
233	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
234	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
235	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
236	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
237	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
238	                __threadfence();
239	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
240	            } else {
241	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
242	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
243	                       == my_gen) {
244	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
245	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
246	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
247	#endif
248	                }
249	            }
250	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
251	        }
252	
253	        __syncthreads();
254	    }
255	};

258	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
259	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
260	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
261	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.

263	struct PersistentContext {
264	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
265	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
266	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
267	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
268	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
269	
270	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
271	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
272	    }
273	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
274	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
275	    }
276	};

352	//    specs live here too (identical for all threads → shared, not per-thread

355	struct DecTcSmem {
356	    // GEMM K-loop ring. The M-atom-interleaved wgmma pipeline stages up to
357	    // kDecAtomsPerSlot A(64×16) tiles per slot (one per stacked m64 atom in an
358	    // interleave GROUP, issued back-to-back into independent fp32 fragments so the
359	    // tensor pipe overlaps them) + ONE shared B(N×16) tile per slot. Layout:
360	    // A-tiles packed [slot][atom-in-group] (slot s, atom ai at
361	    // sA + (s*kDecAtomsPerSlot + ai)*64*16); B [slot] at sB + s*N*16.
362	    // kDecAtomsPerSlot = min(kAtomsM, kDecMaxIL) = the widest interleave group any
363	    // call site uses (fwd/dX = kAtomsM=2; dW = 1). At S=2, =2, N=128 the ring is
364	    // 2·(2·2KB + 4KB)=16KB; DecTcSmem total ~17.5KB ≪ the 48KB static cap.
365	    static constexpr int kDecAtomsPerSlot =
366	        (dectc::kAtomsM < dectc::kDecMaxIL) ? dectc::kAtomsM : dectc::kDecMaxIL;
367	    __nv_bfloat16 sA[dectc::kDecTcStages * kDecAtomsPerSlot * 64 * 16];
368	    __nv_bfloat16 sB[dectc::kDecTcStages * SG_TUNED_TILE_N * 16];
369	    float red[256];
370	    dectc::DecDwSpec spec[9];
371	};

373	// ── TC workspace layout (carved from tok.workspace; the host sizes it for the
374	//    TC path — see dec_tc_workspace_floats). Regions (float units):
375	//      [0 .. acts_f)                      : DecActs bf16 region (reinterpreted)
376	//      [acts_f .. acts_f + nCTA*scratch)  : per-CTA tile scratch (f32)
377	//      [.. + nCTA*kLnVecElems)            : per-CTA LN-vec partials (f32)
378	//      [.. + nCTA)                        : per-CTA loss slots (f32)
379	//      [.. + 1)                           : reduced scalar loss (host reads it)
380	//    acts_f = ceil(acts_bf16 / 2). ──
381	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_acts_floats(int T, int B) {
382	    // mirror dectc::dec_acts_bind's running offset (bf16 elems) → floats.
383	    const int64_t d = dec::kD, dff = dec::kDff, V = dec::kVocab, L = dec::kLayers;
384	    const int64_t Td = (int64_t)T * d, T3d = (int64_t)T * 3 * d, Tff = (int64_t)T * dff;
385	    int64_t bf = 0;
386	    for (int li = 0; li < L; ++li) bf += Td + Td + Td + Tff + T3d + Td + Tff + Td;
387	    bf += (int64_t)B * d + (int64_t)B * V + Td;     // X_hn + dY_logits + dh0
388	    return (bf + 1) / 2;
389	}

415	// stage publishes per-CTA (r,s) slots (2*nCTA) + a reduced-d slot (1) — an owner-

417	// LARGEST nCTA (one CTA/SM = #SMs); tiny (≤ 2*132+1 ≈ 1 KB) and carved

419	// allocates one workspace that fits every OptId. Unused by AdamW/Lion/… (their

421	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_opt_reduce_floats(int nCTA) {
422	    if (!kDecStagedOptScratch) return 0;     // bench (adamw-only): Prodigy never runs
423	    return (int64_t)2 * nCTA + 1;            // [r slots | s slots | reduced d]

426	//    shape to the vit twin (vit_tc_muon_floats): the NS chain runs ONE 2D weight at
427	//    a time over all CTAs; the scratch holds X/A/AX/AAX/orth for the LARGEST 2D weight
